title: Deion Sanders didn't have to testify in the Shilo Sanders bankruptcy trial
summary: Thursday was a good day for Deion Sanders, on two counts.
full_text: Thursday was a good day for Deion Sanders, on two counts. First, his Colorado team upset Georgia Tech to start the season 1-0. Second, the judge presiding over Shilo Sanders's bankruptcy trial decided that Deion wouldn't be required to testify in the case. Via Brent Schrotenboer of USA Today , the presiding judge declared on Thursday that Deion was released from his subpoena . The day didn't go as well in court for Shilo. As Schrotenboer explains, a witness called by Shilo's lawyers offered contradictory testimony on a key question in the case of whether injuries inflicted by Shilo on John Darjean, a security guard at his school, were "willful and malicious." The witness, Ruda Nash James, testified that she saw Darjean choking Shilo. During the testimony, Darjean's lawyer played a recording of a phone call between James and Shilo's mother from the day of the 2015 incident. "Did you see his hand around Shilo’s neck?” Pilar Sanders asked James. “I didn’t see the neck part,” James said. “I didn’t see all that.” Oops. Separately, Shilo's lawyer was stopped by the judge (who will be deciding the case) from questioning Darjean about the possibility that his injuries were the result of his baseball career. As the judge pointed out, the current case isn't about whether the fight with Shilo caused injuries that culminated in an $11.89 million judgment that created the debt Shilo hopes to discharge through bankruptcy. It's only about whether the injuries were willfully or maliciously inflicted. The biggest bit of drama on Thursday happened when Darjean collapsed after testifying, apparently due to his chronic pain. It appears that the case was paused on Friday. Eventually, the judge will decide whether Shilo will, or won't, carry the $11.89 million debt moving forward.
author: Mike Florio

title: Miami Hurricanes linebacker Mohamed Toure starts his eighth year of college football
summary: As controversy about player eligibility embroils college football, LSU has decided not to play two former NFL players today.
full_text: As controversy about player eligibility embroils college football, LSU has decided not to play two former NFL players today. But another player whose eligibility demonstrates major changes in the NCAA was on the field for the Miami Hurricanes' opener on Friday night. Miami linebacker Mohamed Toure recorded five tackles in Friday night's win over Stanford, which is noteworthy because this is Toure's eighth season playing college football. Before transferring to Miami last year, Toure had been on the team at Rutgers for six years. Toure announced in January that he would return to the Hurricanes for the 2026 season, and unlike the issue of former NFL players, there wasn't even any controversy about it because the NCAA made clear that he's eligible for an eighth season — something that once would have been unthinkable in college football. Here's how every year of Toure's college football career has unfolded: In 2019, Toure enrolled at Rutgers and played two games as a freshman. At the time, the rules said that he could take that year as a redshirt and play four more years after that, so his eligibility would be used up after the 2023 season. In 2020, Toure played nine games for Rutgers, but the NCAA decided not to count that season toward any player’s eligibility because of the impact that covid had on the 2020 season. In 2021, Toure played 13 games for Rutgers. As far as the NCAA was concerned, this was the first year that counted toward his four years of eligibility. In 2022, Toure missed the season with an injury. In the old days, the redshirt year he took in 2019 would have meant he couldn’t take another medical redshirt, but under the newer rules, the NCAA didn’t count 2022 toward his eligibility limit. So through four years at Rutgers, he had still used only one year of NCAA eligibility. In 2023, Toure played 13 games for Rutgers. This previously would have been his final year of eligibility, but the NCAA now calls that only the second year that counted toward his eligibility. In 2024, Toure again missed the season with an injury. The NCAA once again allowed that to be yet another medical redshirt year that didn’t count toward his eligibility, so after his sixth year in college football he had still only used two years of eligibility. In 2025, Toure transferred after six years at Rutgers to Miami, where he was a team captain who helped the Hurricanes get to the College Football National Championship Game. That was his seventh year in college football and his third year of eligibility. And now in 2026, Toure is one of the Hurricanes' top players, in his eighth year of college football and his fourth and — we think — final year of NCAA eligibility.
author: Michael David Smith

title: RedZone Channel is no longer commercial-free, but Scott Hanson promises fewer commercials
summary: For years, host Scott Hanson introduced NFL RedZone Channel by welcoming viewers to "Seven hours of commercial-free football."
full_text: For years, host Scott Hanson introduced NFL RedZone Channel by welcoming viewers to "Seven hours of commercial-free football." That all changed when the NFL decided to make even more money by selling ads on the product, which viewers are already paying to watch. Fans were unhappy, for an obvious reason: The commercials represented billionaire NFL owners enriching themselves at the cost of the quality of the fans' experience. The commercials aren't going away, but Hanson says there will be fewer of them this year. “I could tell you from where we ended last year, there will not be more,” Hanson told Baker Machado of Front Office Sports. “In fact, the actual ads that you see, there will be fewer of what we call the 15-second commercials with the audio going and the product and whatnot.” Hanson said the promos from sponsors he reads will be a major element of RedZone. “Because we’ve done things like the ‘Mercedes-Benz Drive of the Day’ or the ‘Allstate Good Hands Play of the Day’—we’ve done those things, but that’s not considered an outright commercial,” Hanson said. “But the 15-second, ‘okay, we’re on the Dallas Cowboys, first and 10, they get five yards, they’re walking back to the huddle, and then we interject that 15 second standalone commercial?’ There will be fewer at the beginning of the year this year than we ended with at the end of last year. I can confirm that.” That's a step in the right direction, but the right move would be for RedZone Channel to go back to what made it great in the first place: No commercial breaks, and uninterrupted football for fans who love the sport so much they don't want to miss a moment. Those are the fans the NFL should appreciate most, but those fans still don't have seven hours of commercial-free football anymore.
author: Michael David Smith

title: LSU blinks, for now, on the issue of putting former NFL players on the roster
summary: Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris weren't added to the team by Friday's deadline.
full_text: Discretion is the better part of valor. Or something. Despite an injunction allowing LSU to add former NFL players Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris to the roster before Saturday's season opener against Clemson, LSU opted not to do so , via Pete Thamel of ESPN, before the Friday night deadline. The roster has 103 players, leaving two spots for Wright and Harris. Thamel adds that the two players could be added later in the season. The move suggests that LSU took a broader look at the benefits and the cost of moving forward with the two former NFL players, given the intense reaction by the SEC — and the potential for long-term issues with the conference and its other members. The outcome was lurking between the lines of the statement issued on Friday by LSU president Wade Rousse. And while coach Lane Kiffin may have wanted to shout "damn the torpedoes," Rousse apparently realized that the situation could sink the school's future in the SEC. Was it worth it? LSU decided that, for now, it was not.
author: Mike Florio

title: Yes, college football players are already professionals
summary: In 1975, Walter Payton ran roughshod against the Steelers in the annual game that pitted a college all-star team against the defending NFL champions.
full_text: In 1975, Walter Payton ran roughshod against the Steelers in the annual game that pitted a college all-star team against the defending NFL champions. A half-century later, the prospect of any player who ever wore an NFL helmet competing against college players has prompted widespread pearl clutching. It's a weak position. The players who want to return to LSU (and Indiana) aren't hoping to don raccoon coats and chant "boola boola." They simply want to make more money than they'd make on a practice squad. The entire argument that pro players are playing against amateurs is flawed. College players are professional players. For years, they were unpaid professionals. Finally, they're getting fair value. Rece Davis of ESPN made the "college players are professional players" argument on Friday. Which is refreshing, given ESPN's clear interest in doing the bidding of a college system that hopes to parlay a nonsensical argument into a federal antitrust exemption. And it will be very interesting to see whether College GameDay colleagues agree with him on Saturday morning — especially since Nick Saban once brought free-agent NFL running back Trent Richardson back to Alabama to serve as the scout-team running back at practice against the Crimson Tide defense. Either way, the idea that the fairly small universe of players who spent time on NFL rosters should not receive the fifth year of eligibility that all players will get moving forward is, in a word, bullshit. Anyone who loudly makes the case otherwise is, intentionally or not, buying in to the effort to use this isolated, one-year aberration created by the NCAA as fuel to rig the system in a way that hurts all players moving forward.
author: Mike Florio

title: TCU restores credentials to Fort Worth Star-Telegram
summary: It's been a strange week or so when it comes to major football programs removing credentials from reporters.
full_text: It's been a strange week or so when it comes to major football programs removing credentials from reporters. The Titans stripped the credential of Jared Stillman, an independent operator and a part-time presence on the beat who apparently irked the team by engaging in a blunt back-and-forth with quarterback Cam Ward. At the college level, TCU removed the credentials of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . On Friday, TCU reversed its revocation decision. The move happened in bush-league style, with TCU reacting negatively to the Star-Telegram reporting on the locker-room incident between former TCU safety Jacob Fields and receiver Dozie Ezukanma. The incident put Ezukanma in the hospital for three days, with a concussion and a brain bleed. Via Adam Rittenberg of ESPN, TCU said that it had "a series of productive discussions" with the Star-Telegram regarding its coverage. "We made clear our position and resolved to move forward," TCU said. "We respect their role as an independent news source and voice in our community, and we look forward to the season ahead ." TCU took exception to the initial reporting from the Star-Telegram about the incident, because it suggested that the situation extended beyond Fields. The Star-Telegram later revised its reporting, explaining that the attack was not motivated by bullying. And, after the credentials were revoked, the Star-Telegram published an extensive report regarding the situation . Regardless, the answer to a disagreement regarding a given report isn't to yank the publication's credentials. That comes off as heavy-handed and small. There are other avenues for reacting to a dispute, short of invoking the nuclear "you're no longer welcome here" option. The problem, especially at a time when teams and leagues operate their own media outlets and/or own a piece of massive media outlets (e.g., the NFL's 10-percent stake in ESPN), is that teams and leagues believe they can dictate the manner in which they are covered. It should never be that way; media outlets aren't an extension of the P.R. operation. All coverage of a team or a league amounts to free publicity. That alone should make teams and leagues far less willing to piss and moan and far more willing to embrace and show at least a shred of gratitude to anyone and everyone who is willing to help the effort to advertise their product at no charge.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles have seven captains, with none from special teams
summary: Like last year, the Eagles have five offensive captains.
full_text: Like last year, the Eagles have five offensive captains. Like last year, the Eagles have two defensive captains. Unlike last year, the Eagles have no special-teams captains. The Eagles announced their seven 2026 captains on Friday: quarterback Jalen Hurts, running back Saquon Barkley, receiver DeVonta Smith, tackle Lane Johnson, tackle Jordan Mailata, linebacker Zack Baun, and defensive tackle Jordan Davis. Smith replaces receiver A.J. Brown, and Davis replaces safety Reed Blankenship. No one replaces kicker Jake Elliott, who wore a 'C' in 2025. Davis is the only first-time captain. Hurts has won the distinction for a fifth straight year. Most teams have at least one special-teams captain. Some teams prefer not to potentially distract a kicker's pregame ritual with any additional responsibilities that come from being a game-day captain.
author: Mike Florio

title: After getting shot in February, 49ers DE Keion White is good to go
summary: The very strange 2026 for the 49ers included the February shooting of defensive end Keion White in a San Francisco bar and nightclub, which reportedly happened after the rapper Lil Baby and White got into an argument when Lil Baby's entourage tried to enter White's private party.
full_text: '' The very strange 2026 for the 49ers included the February shooting of defensive end Keion White in a San Francisco bar and nightclub, which reportedly happened after the rapper Lil Baby and White got into an argument when Lil Baby's entourage tried to enter White's private party. White recently spoke about his recovery from the shooting, in an interview with Vic Tafur of The Athletic . “It’s different because it’s trauma instead of just, like, breaking an ankle with a sports-related injury,” White told Tafur earlier this week. “When you hurt yourself in football, there’s a protocol for damn near everything. Football players don’t just get shot every day. . . . I mean, I guess they do on this team ." White was making a joke of sorts regarding the fact that, two years ago on Labor Day weekend, receiver Ricky Pearsall was shot during a robbery attempt in San Francisco. “It was a gunshot to the foot,” White said regarding his injury. “I broke my talus bone, so I had to have surgery — two screws in there. But, yeah, brush it off. [I] literally was making jokes as I was going to the hospital.” White told Tafur he never feared for his life; however, White reportedly has declined to identify the shooter. “The funny part is, I was actually the one calming everybody else down,” White said. “I don’t really take a lot of things seriously. I didn’t even know I got shot until like five minutes after, as I was walking around.” White's attempt to downplay the situation included a joke about a past injury to the other foot that required screws. “I got screws in each ankle now, so I’m symmetrical," White said. He said that it was a "touch-and-go situation right up to the beginning of training camp," but he has been able to practice and is ready to play. As Tafur explains, the 49ers need White to play and play well. As the regular season approaches, defensive end Mykel Williams (knee) is out, Nick Bosa (knee) is still recovering from his latest ACL tear, Sam Okuayinonu (foot) is out, and rookie Romello Height has an ankle issue.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ongoing UNC investigation could take out Bill Belichick, for cause
summary: Question of whether Belichick knew about, and didn't report, certain issues under investigation could bring him down.
full_text: North Carolina G.M. Michael Lombardi resigned on Thursday , not long before a sweeping report from WRAL painted an ugly picture of the Tar Heels program. Defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, based on that report, could be next . The eventual target could be coach Bill Belichick, also in a for-cause, you'll-get-nothing-and-like-it outcome that would wipe out the remainder of his buyout. Here's the key portion of the WRAL report, as it relates to accounts from individuals who have been questioned by an external law firm: "[T]he people said they were asked whether they had reported any potentially questionable behavior to Bill Belichick ." That's an important potential finding, as it relates to Article 11 of Bill Belichick's five-year, $50 million deal. The provision sets forth the various ways in which Belichick can be fired for cause. The key language appears in Article 11(c): "Any action that is (i) taken by Coach or someone supervised by Coach, or (ii) taken at the direction of Coach or someone supervised by Coach, or (iii) known by Coach or someone supervised by Coach and not reported by Coach as required by this Agreement to the Department of Athletics Compliance office by the person supervised by coach, and that results in any material form of disciplinary finding, material action against, or material sanction for the Coach or the Program by the University's athletics association (e.g. NCAA), athletics conference (e.g. ACC), University, or other regulatory body that exceeds an institutional letter of admonishment or reprimand." (Emphasis added.) Given the potentially serious subjects currently under investigation (reportedly including whether Steve Belichick “used drugs on the job or provided drugs to at least one player," whether an unnamed member of the North Carolina recruiting staff had a sexual relationship with a player, and whether assistant coaches and the recruiting staff engaged in sexual relationships), a finding that Bill Belichick knew about one or more of those matters and failed to report them could provide the basis to fire him for cause, and in turn to cut off his buyout. The mere existence of the investigation suggests that someone within the UNC power structure may be looking for a reason to fire Belichick for cause. At plenty of schools where the program is winning, the inclination will be to look the other way when evidence of potential violations emerges. Only when management is looking for a way out do the chapters and verses of the contract's termination provision become a priority.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McDermott sees the Bills getting to the Super Bowl in 2026
summary: The Bills fired coach Sean McDermott two days after an overtime loss to the Broncos in the divisional round of the playoffs.
full_text: ' The Bills fired coach Sean McDermott two days after an overtime loss to the Broncos in the divisional round of the playoffs. That's not stopping McDermott from rooting for his former team — or from believing that they can get farther in the first year after his exit than McDermott took them in nine seasons on the job. "With what they've done, the moves that Brandon Beane has made, and the activity they've had on the roster, just so over the last, you know, 'X' amount of months has, I think, been very important," McDermott told Rich Eisen on Friday. "And so I think, if you're betting on the Super Bowl contender, they're certainly one of them. I don't see why, you know, why you wouldn’t bet on them ? Because the games, at the end of the day, have to be played, right? It's one thing on paper, but it's another thing to play the gams." Eisen asked whether this means McDermott envisions a Rams-Bills Super Bowl, which would be a rematch of their Week 5 Monday night showdown. "It';; be Bills-Rams," McDermott said. "It'd be a great Super Bowl. Those Rams. Listen, people ask me all the time, 'Hey, do you still root for your old team?' And I said, 'Why wouldn't I?' Right? Of course I do. I mean, the impact that you want to have as a head coach on a team and a community, that's one thing. But, man oh man, the impact that that team, that building, and that community had on me and my family, we'll remember that for the rest of our lives, Rich, and that's part of sports, right? The wins and the losses are important, but it's, like, the impact you leave, or that is left on people and the fan base and them on you, and that's the real part of sports." In the NFL, the real part of the game is that plenty of coaches are shown the door, after every season. McDermott was one of 10 who left, voluntarily or otherwise, after the 2025 season. And he's clearly hoping that, after the 2026 season, he'll have a chance to fill one of the inevitable vacancies to come. Which means that his freedom to root for the Bills and only the Bills may be short-lived. Come 2027, McDermott could be coaching another team in the AFC — and possibly another team in the AFC East, if there's eventually an opening with the Jets.
author: Mike Florio

title: Two Indiana players get TRO to return for 2026
summary: Curt Cignetti apparently is an agent of chaos, too.
full_text: Curt Cignetti apparently is an agent of chaos, too. With so much focus on the apparent intention of LSU coach Lane Kiffin to bring back players who spent time with 90-man NFL rosters, a pair of Indiana players won a ruling on Friday that allows them to return to the school. Via ESPN, Judge Kara Krothe issued the temporary restraining order prohibiting the NCAA and any conferences from prohibiting the players from competing during the 2026-27 season. Wrote Judge Krothe: "To be clear, it is the Court's intention to place Plaintiffs in the position they were in at the end of their last college sports season. As long as they would have been eligible, academically and otherwise, to continue playing college sports in the following semester if they had a fifth year of eligibility, they are eligible today ." Another hearing is set for September 11. The players, Stephen Daley and Kellan Wyatt, returned to the Indiana program in early August, but their status wasn't clear until Friday. The Big Ten has yet to deal with Indiana in the same way that the SEC has dealt with LSU, with lots of huffing and puffing and the lingering possibility that the SEC will blow the Tigers out of the conference. The Hoosier start their season on Saturday, against North Texas. It's unclear whether Daley and Wyatt will play.
author: Mike Florio

title: As Aaron Rodgers plans to retire, the next step is fatherhood
summary: Aaron Rodgers will retire from football after the upcoming season.
full_text: '' Aaron Rodgers will retire from football after the upcoming season. Which means that, when the next season gets started n 2027 (blink your eyes and it'll be here), he'll be doing something other than playing football. So what will he be doing? Adam Schein of SiriusXM Mad Dog Radio posed that question to Rodgers on Friday. “I'm hopefully going to be supporting my pregnant wife because we're going to start a family and I am not going to be making a lot of appearances or statements," Rodgers told Schein. "And I'm looking forward to a life of quiet after 22 years in the pros and three in college and getting my body healed up and working on a family. That's what I'm looking forward to." The answer marks a subtle shift from his prior insistence that we won't see or hear from him at all after he stops playing. “When this is done, it’s Keyser Soze, and you won’t see me ,” Rodgers said in March 2026. “You won’t see me. I’m not doing TV. . . . I’m not gonna be out and about.” Regardless, Rodgers is looking forward to having a Keyser Soze Jr. “I'm definitely excited about it," Rodgers told Schein. "I mean, being back in my family's lives and I'm having a lot of fun being Uncle Aaron. I mean, I have a few godkids that I'm involved with, but being Uncle Aaron to my brother's kids has been a lot of fun. And the more I'm around them, the more I get excited and so does the wife about having some of our own. So, yeah, I'm excited for that. I can't wait for that next chapter of life and all that that entails, and sleepless nights and crying babies and changing diapers and all those things. I'm looking forward to all of it.” Those of us who have dealt with sleepless nights and crying babies and changing diapers think that's cute. The intended timetable is clear: “I'm talking about I'm hoping that I have a pregnant wife by next [year] this time." Those of us who have learned, both ways, that it doesn't always work that way think that's cute, too. Regardless, the clock is ticking. Rodgers is 42. And no one knows his wife's age. Few know her name. Or what she looks like. Maybe she's Keyser Soze.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: 49ers to sign DE Khalid Kareem to active roster
summary: The 49ers are adding some help at defensive end ahead of their season opener in Australia.
full_text: '' The 49ers are adding some help at defensive end ahead of their season opener in Australia. Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports that they are signing Khalid Kareem off of the Falcons' practice squad. Kareem was on the Falcons the last two years and returned to the team after being released by the Giants last weekend. 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris was the head coach in Atlanta during Kareem's two seasons with the team. He had 11 tackles in six regular season appearances for the Falcons. Kareem also played in 28 games for the Bears, Colts, and Bengals. The 49ers announced that Sam Okuayinonu will not play against the Rams on Thursday and they have not yet said if Nick Bosa will play after tearing his ACL last season. Keion White and third-round pick Romello Height are the other defensive ends on their active roster.
author: Josh Alper

title: Michael Wilson: I wanted to stay in Arizona to be a centerpiece of turnaround
summary: Cardinals wide receiver Michael Wilson got his long-awaited contract extension this week, keeping him under contract through the 2029 season.
full_text: Cardinals wide receiver Michael Wilson got his long-awaited contract extension this week, keeping him under contract through the 2029 season. It is what he wanted. "I want to be a centerpiece of trying to flip something," Wilson said, via Darren Urban of the team website. "That's way more gratifying and rewarding going through the dark days and tough times when you've lost bad games, when there is more Niner fans than Arizona fans [in the stands]. How cool would it be . . . when we are in the race of the playoffs or a playoff team or in the playoffs and being a centerpiece of turning the tides? That sense of loyalty, that just screams the type of player and person I want to be. "I've got so much love for Arizona. Not even tied to the franchise, I could see myself living here the rest of my life." While letting his agent handle contract talks, Wilson wasn't sure the deal would get done before the start of the season. A report Wednesday morning indicated a deal was unlikely, with Wilson set to enter free agency in March. Wilson saw the report. "Conversations happened, tides turned and things got done," Wilson said. "I couldn't even sleep [with excitement after the deal got done Wednesday night]." Wilson caught 85 passes for 1,113 yards and seven touchdowns over his first two seasons. The Cardinals wide receiver had 78 receptions for 1,006 yards and seven touchdowns last season. The team sees him as part of the foundation for the rebuild. "His approach every single day, it's just so consistent," coach Mike LaFleur said. "It's the meeting rooms, his attention to detail, just how he goes about his business. He's the perfect example of, 'Don't mistake his kindness for weakness.' This dude is a tough dude, and I've gotten to see a little bit more. I knew it, and I've seen it, but then you get to see it even a little bit more during competition."
author: Charean Williams

title: S Taylor Rapp worked out for the Broncos
summary: When safety Taylor Rapp was released by the Broncos in August, the team left the door open for a return.
full_text: When safety Taylor Rapp was released by the Broncos in August, the team left the door open for a return. Head coach Sean Payton said that Rapp told the team needed "a little time at home" shortly after signing and that there was " a better than good chance " that he would return to the Broncos at a later date. That date may not be too far into the future. The NFL's transaction report for Friday shows that Rapp worked out for the team. Any return would likely begin via the practice squad, which would give Rapp a chance to work with the team and potentially be activated on gameday. Rapp appeared in six games for the Bills last season and has made 57 career appearances for the Bills and the Rams.
author: Josh Alper

title: Falcons sign LB Bralen Trice back to practice squad
summary: The Falcons signed linebacker Bralen Trice to the practice squad, the team announced.
full_text: The Falcons signed linebacker Bralen Trice to the practice squad, the team announced. Atlanta drafted Trice in the third round in 2024, but he has not played a game for the Falcons yet. The team waived him on Sunday. Trice, 25, tore his ACL in his first preseason game and missed his entire rookie year. He then aggravated the same knee in 2025 and didn't play last season either. Trice was a two-time first-team All-Pac-12 selection at Washington and a two-time bowl game MVP.
author: Charean Williams

title: Sean McVay: I look at Stetson Bennett, Ty Simpson as "2A, 2B"
summary: The Rams released a depth chart that shows Stetson Bennett as the team's second quarterback and first-round pick Ty Simpson as their third quarterback, but head coach Sean McVay said things are less clear cut than that would make it appear.
full_text: The Rams released a depth chart that shows Stetson Bennett as the team's second quarterback and first-round pick Ty Simpson as their third quarterback, but head coach Sean McVay said things are less clear cut than that would make it appear. McVay said that he has not made a decision about who will be active for Thursday's game against the 49ers because he views the two quarterbacks on equal footing when it comes to the competition to be the next man up behind Matthew Stafford. "I'll tell you when I decide who is going to be the actual two in the game," McVay said, via the team's website. "I've talked to the players about it, but that's something that they're both going to continue to train regardless of who it ends up being up and who is the emergency third. I look at it as both of those guys are going to play, but you saw, we listed Stetson as the two, Ty as the three. But I look at it as the 2A, 2B and we'll see how we approach the game." McVay added that he doesn't "want to necessarily say that whatever we do in Week 1 is how it stays throughout the year," so the backup spot could be a fluid one and the Rams will be hoping that neither player sees the field outside of garbage time between now and February.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys' captains: Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, Dak Prescott, Brandon Aubrey
summary: The Cowboys have two defensive captains this season, and both were acquired by trading Micah Parsons.
full_text: The Cowboys have two defensive captains this season, and both were acquired by trading Micah Parsons. Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams are the Cowboys' defensive captains. A year ago, the Cowboys traded Parsons to the Packers for Clark and two first-round picks, and later they traded one of those picks to the Jets for Williams. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer singled out Williams as a leader who has meant a lot to the team. "From the minute he got here, he's been about one thing, and it's winning," Schottenheimer said of Williams. "He's never won in the NFL and the leadership is real, the talent is incredible, but every decision that guy makes is based on what's best for us winning. I love that about him, and it's infectious. It rubs off. I love hearing him talk to the young linemen, the young defenders." Unsurprisingly, quarterback Dak Prescott is the offensive captain and kicker Brandon Aubrey is the special teams captain. Schottenheimer said the players voted on the captains, and those four players were overwhelmingly the top vote getters. "All player voting, and that's what I think makes it such an awesome, incredible designation, that you get voted on by the players, your peers, your brothers," Schottenheimer said. "Those guys were clearly the four highest, and that spoke volumes to me when I looked at the numbers."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Josh Jacobs's first court appearance moves from November 17 to September 10
summary: Paid leave puts a premium on expediting the prosecuion.
full_text: With Packers running back Josh Jacobs on paid leave in light of multiple misdemeanor charges (including battery), time is of the essence when it comes to resolving the criminal case. And the presiding judge apparently has accommodated Jacobs's urgency. Via Michael Gross of Fox 11, Jacobs's initial court appearance has been moved from November 17 to September 10 . Typically, a player remains on paid leave until the case ends, and then until the NFL imposes discipline. It's possible, however, for the player to be sidelined for the anticipated duration of his eventual suspension, with credit later given for any game missed (and the salary earned forfeited). The safest approach for Jacobs will be to get the situation wrapped up. Beyond the expedited hearing, it's possible a prompt plea deal will be reached.
author: Mike Florio

title: Shaq Mason won't be disciplined after 2025 arrest, remains a free agent
summary: Shaq Mason is ready to resume his career.
full_text: Shaq Mason is ready to resume his career. Via Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, Mason was informed by the NFLPA that he will not face discipline from the league stemming from his 2025 arrest. While Mason was facing allegations of an alleged domestic assault and was arrested in Aug. 2025, all charges were subsequently dropped in April of this year. The investigation into his legal matters is now closed. Mason was released by the Texans in March 2025 and was not with a team last year. A fourth-round pick in 2015, Mason spent his first seven seasons with the Patriots, winning two Super Bowls. He then played for Tampa Bay in 2022 — reuniting with Tom Brady — before heading suiting up for Houston in 2023 and 2024. Mason has appeared in 152 games with 147 starts in his career. He remains a free agent who is eligible to immediately sign with a club.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Clemson tells LSU that use of former NFL players could breach game contract
summary: As the SEC and LSU continue to battle over whether the Tigers will use former NFL players in Saturday night's regular-season opener, LSU's opponent has chimed in.
full_text: As the SEC and LSU continue to battle over whether the Tigers will use former NFL players in Saturday night's regular-season opener, LSU's opponent has chimed in. Via Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports, Clemson has informed LSU that playing former professional players on Saturday may constitute a breach of the game contract. That said, Clemson said it intends to play the game — and that it is not seeking financial damages. Obvious question: Why raise it if they're not going to do anything about it? Obvious answer: It's another piece of performative nonsense aimed at getting a federal antitrust exemption. And here's the final point for now, one that was made on Friday's PFT Live . Why are college teams making an issue out of using "professional" players? Currently, college football players are professional players . The guys who want to return to LSU aren't doing it because they're choosing to eschew the riches of the NFL in an effort to win a national title. Playing for LSU pays them better than they'd be paid as members of a pro team's practice squad.
author: Mike Florio

title: The Falcons still don't have a starting quarterback (but will soon)
summary: With the first game of the season only nine days away, the Falcons still haven't named a starting quarterback.
full_text: With the first game of the season only nine days away, the Falcons still haven't named a starting quarterback. The competition, ostensibly, is between Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr. But how, as Simms said on Thursday's PFT Live , can it be a competition when Penix hasn't been able to compete? The Falcons published their weekly media schedule on Friday, and there will be a "starting quarterback press conference" next Wednesday. Obviously, the identity of the starter will be known by then. Our guess is that it will happen early in the week, probably on Monday, with the announcement coming Tuesday morning at the earliest. And if Penix still isn't ready to go as he continues to recover from a torn ACL, the likely options are Tua and Cooper Rush. (I'd roll the dice with undrafted rookie Jack Strand, but that's possibly one of the many reasons why I don't run a team.) Here's where the situation can get very interesting. If the Falcons decide to go with Rush, who is 9-7 in 16 career starts, why even keep Tua on the team? His $1.215 million base salary isn't guaranteed. They could cut him, and he'd still get the full $54 million he's owed by the Dolphins for 2026. It made sense to sign Tua. He was cheap. He beat the Falcons in Atlanta last year. When everything is working as planned, he can perform at a high level. When, however, things go sideways ( e.g. , if the first read isn't there), Tua tends to get happy feet. The Falcons gave it a try. Tua gave it a try. If he can't beat out Rush for the Week 1 start in Pittsburgh (where Tua made his last start for the Dolphins last December), there's no reason to keep him on the roster. Frankly, if Tua falls behind Rush, Tua shouldn't want to stay.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Donald's status for Week 1 still TBD, all players set to travel to Australia
summary: At this point, it's still unclear whether or not Aaron Donald will play when the Rams take on the 49ers next week to open the 2026 season.
full_text: At this point, it's still unclear whether or not Aaron Donald will play when the Rams take on the 49ers next week to open the 2026 season. But he will at least be on the scene. Via Benjamin Royer of the Southern California News Group, head coach Sean McVay said on Friday that all players — including Donald — are expected to travel to Australia. But Donald’s playing status is still to be determined, with McVay noting he “ doesn’t have that sense quite yet .” Donald officially elected to end his retirement and return to the Rams on Sunday. He’s been in and out of practice since then, though he said he’s been training for around 13-14 weeks to put himself in a position to play again. Donald retired after the 2023 season. While the 49ers are already in Australia acclimating to the significant time difference, the Rams are taking a much different approach by traveling just before the day of the game.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Experts sound off on failed grass field at new Bills stadium
summary: Carl Spackler is having his day.
full_text: Carl Spackler is having his day. With the Bills ripping up the grass at their new stadium after only two preseason games and installing a new one for the regular-season home opener, various grass experts have sounded off. Tim Graham of The Athletic has collected and published their comments . The legendary George Toma said this as to the failed field: “That hurts me. That’s terrible to happen at all, but so soon? Somebody fell asleep.” Another "award-winning sports agronomist" with extensive experience installing pro and college surfaces, but who requested anonymity for apparent fear of Big Sod, said that it was "the worst sod I’ve seen in the NFL in my career. I can’t even imagine how that could have happened." Added Tony Dick, sports management professor at Baldwin Wallace University and former Cleveland Browns assistant head groundskeeper: "[N]atural turf is safer in a perfect setting. But if you have the situation like you have in Buffalo — and I went back and watched the film — you cannot tell me that field was safer than the artificial turf they just left. . . . I’m never putting Josh Allen on a field in that condition.” The Bills had this to say about the issue, via Graham: “We have consulted with the NFL and an independent expert who works with multiple NFL teams. These consultants recommended utilizing this three-week window before the home opener to install the sod. The NFL inspects every field and determines whether it meets league standards. We are confident that they are the appropriate group to ensure the field performs at the necessary level.” Still, the unnamed agronomist is skeptical. “They will have a difficult time,” he said. “There’s so much going wrong, and there’s so little time. If that field makes it through the second game, I’ll be shocked.” Professor Dick offered a prediction: "You might have artificial turf back in there within three years, just because it’s safer than whatever that was." The first test of Sod 2.0 is only 13 days away. That's when the Bills host the Lions, the first of three Buffalo games in three weekends.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jayden Daniels: I can't live off what I did in 2024
summary: The discussion around Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels this summer has been focused more on his jersey number at LSU than anything having to do with his current play, but that will change next weekend.
full_text: The discussion around Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels this summer has been focused more on his jersey number at LSU than anything having to do with his current play, but that will change next weekend. Daniels will make his first start since Week 14 of last season when the Commanders face the Eagles in Week 1 and he'll be making his first start since the Commanders replaced offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury with David Blough. When Daniels does take the field, people will be watching to see how he runs an offense that has him under center and huddling more often than in the past as well as whether he can be the dynamic player he was as a rookie without the injuries that swamped his 2025 season. In an interview with Albert Breer of SI.com, Daniels acknowledged those questions and that he has to show he has grown as a player since taking the Commanders to the 2024 NFC Championship Game. “Out of sight, out of mind,” Daniels said. “A lot of people, what they last saw was me getting hurt, so what can I say? I can’t live off of what was done in ’24. Obviously, salute to the other guys in my class. Drake [Maye] did what he did. So did Caleb [Williams]. So did Bo [Nix]. Hopefully, down the line, we can go down as the greatest QB class. I know we have a long way to go, but shout out to them, honestly. So I have a chance, when I get out there, in Week 1, to showcase my talents once again, and remind a lot of people.” The ultimate success of the Commanders will come down to more than just how Daniels performs, but the quarterback's play will have a lot to do with how the overall trajectory of the franchise is viewed after a smashing start came to a crashing end last year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Hall of Fame overhauls voting process, reducing panel from 50 to 28
summary: The Belichick snub has prompted major changes to the rules.
full_text: The inexplicable snub of Bill Belichick has sparked significant changes. Whether those changes will make the Hall of Fame voting process better is unclear, for now. The Pro Football Hall of Fame has revised its bylaws with the intent of improving the selection process. The changes will overhaul the process by (among other things) reducing the panel of voters from 50 to 28 and limiting eligibility to three categories: players, coaches, and contributors. The announcement from the Hall of Fame contends that a comprehensive review started 2.5 years ago. Common sense says that the embarrassment arising from the failure of Belichick to make the cut was the catalyst. The new bylaws eliminate the seniors category, keeping all players in the same pool without an artificial 25-year window for the "modern era." This eliminates what has necessarily become a cleanup process by giving out one or more busts per year to players who failed to make it during their quarter century of eligibility. The revamped selection committee ditches a model that consisted of one voter per team, 17 at-large voters, and one representative of the Pro Football Writers of America. The new panel will consist of 27 at-large voters and a PFWA representative. While making each vote more meaningful, the chance prevents (ideally) the presence of voters who no longer actively cover the NFL as their primary employment. At the annual selection meeting, the 28 voters will consider 13 players, one coach, and one contributor, with the coach and the contributor finalists determined by a separate committee. The contributor category has been expanded from those who contribute to the game beyond playing or coaching to examining a person's full football résumé: playing, coaching, and other contributions. This provides an avenue for candidates like John Madden (who technically got in as a coach but whose enshrinement surely was fueled by is broadcasting career and video-game franchise) and Dick LeBeau (who technically got in as a player but who was better known as a coach) to have a separate, and perhaps easier, path to induction. (That said, it also makes it harder for owners and non-General Managers to get in, since they'll be competing against players and coaches who have done more than that.) The meeting will change, too. Instead of assigning specific voters to present the candidates, the same person will present all of them — and that person won't be a voter. This revision eliminates disparities in the "skills of the individuals making the presentations," and it prevents one specific voter from becoming an open and obvious advocate for the candidate. The value of the changes ultimately comes down to the identity of the voters. The Hall of Fame has not yet announced the new panel.
author: Mike Florio

title: Brock Purdy: Playing in NFC West means we have to be at our best every moment
summary: It doesn't take much effort to come up with an argument for the NFC West being the toughest division in the NFL.
full_text: '' It doesn't take much effort to come up with an argument for the NFC West being the toughest division in the NFL. The Seahawks beat the Rams and 49ers in the playoffs on their way to winning the Super Bowl last year. The Rams responded to that by trading for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie ahead of Aaron Donald's return from retirement, which has made them slight favorites over Seattle to wind up winning the NFC. The 49ers are hoping for better health than they enjoyed while winning 12 games last season and quarterback Brock Purdy laid out to Matt Maiocco of NBCSportsBayArea.com just why that will be so important. “We have an extremely competitive, great division,” Purdy said. “I think the best in the NFL. And that excites us because you got to be your best at every moment, every play, every drive. Every game matters, every little thing matters. It all adds up and we even saw it last year.” Purdy and the Niners won't have to wait long to test themselves against a divisional foe. They'll kick off the season against the Rams in Melbourne on Thursday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Brian Schottenheimer says he's "elated" to have Joe Milton on Cowboys' practice squad
summary: When the Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, they knew they wanted him back on the practice squad, but they weren't sure if another team would claim him on waivers, or persuade him to join a different practice squad.
full_text: When the Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, they knew they wanted him back on the practice squad, but they weren't sure if another team would claim him on waivers, or persuade him to join a different practice squad. For coach Brian Schottenheimer, Milton deciding to stay in Dallas was great news. "When he informed me he's coming back, I was elated," Schottenheimer said. "This is a guy that's worked his butt off to get where he is, developed the way he's developed. The talent is so rare. When you're waived — I've been fired many times — you're in shock a little bit. Then you step back and you didn't see it coming, but you start figuring out the positives and negatives of the situation. For him to be able to stay here with the relationships he's built, understanding our system, understanding the locker room, the other coaches, we were thrilled to get him back and he's going to continue to get better." Schottenheimer knows there's always a chance that some other team will sign Milton away for its active roster. "Quarterback rooms around the league are pretty crowded right now, but he's certainly talented enough to get claimed. It's our good fortune that he wasn't," Schottenheimer said. Milton's size, speed and arm strength make him a very attractive prospect, even if so far he hasn't put it all together to develop into a starting quarterback. The Cowboys think he's going to keep developing and they're glad he's doing it in Dallas.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Vrabel: Christian Gonzalez situation hasn't been a distraction
summary: With the season opener rapidly approaching, it's still unclear whether Gonzalez will get a new deal — or if he'll play if he doesn't.
full_text: The Patriots and Seahawks will open the 2026 season next Wednesday. At this point, it's still unclear whether or not cornerback Christian Gonzalez will be on the field for the contest. While the Patriots and Gonzalez have been locked in a contract dispute, head coach Mike Vrabel said on Friday that he doesn't feel like the situation has been a distraction. “No. When Christian was rehabbing, he was where he was supposed to be when he was supposed to be there. Talked about his professionalism. I can’t speak for the rest of the team and how they feel ,” Vrabel said in his weekly interview with WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show . “From a coaching staff standpoint, it’s this: who is available each day, and we go about making a practice plan, or this is what the reps are going to be this day. We deal with all different kinds of things each and every day about who is available and who is not available. So I can only speak for myself, and it hasn’t been a distraction. I try to coach everybody that is here each and every day.” Vrabel said the Patriots will be ready whether or not Gonzalez plays. “We’ll have multiple game plans based on what the down and distance is, what personnel they are in, how the game may unfold,” Vrabel said. “We have to be flexible and be willing and ready to adjust. That’ll never change.” For his part, Gonzalez told reporters on Thursday that he’s “still frustrated” by the situation and did not commit to playing in the season opener. “I mean, when that time comes, that’s when things will happen ,” Gonzalez said, via Karen Guregian of MassLive.com, noting that there are still several days for the two sides to come to an agreement. “We’ll save that [answer] for when it’s game time.” The No. 17 overall pick of the 2023 draft, Gonzalez has recorded 24 passes defensed and three interceptions in 34 games over his first three seasons.

title: Agent's Take: How the Rams built a salary-cap super team around Matthew Stafford
summary: Here's how the Rams fit their stars under the salary cap and what the spending spree means for their future
full_text:
A 31-27 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship Game was considered by the Los Angeles Rams as a missed opportunity because their NFC West divisional rival dominated the New England Patriots to win Super Bowl LX. Once 2025 NFL MVP Matthew Stafford quickly decided to return for an 18th season, the Rams swung for the fences to capitalize.
The only unrestricted free agent of consequence was safety Kam Curl. He was retained on a three-year, $36 million contract, with up to $39 million in salary escalators.
Cornerback, the most glaring roster weakness, was upgraded in a trade and through free agency. Trent McDuffie , who was entering a contract year, was acquired from the Kansas City Chiefs in March. He signed a four-year, $124 million contract extension in connection with the trade, making him the NFL's highest-paid cornerback at the time. Jaylen Watson , McDuffie's cornerback counterpart in Kansas City, received a three-year, $51 million deal as an unrestricted free agent.
Another order of business was adjusting Stafford's contract. As the 2025 NFL MVP, Stafford was still underpaid despite renegotiating the final two years of the four-year, $160 million extension he signed in 2022, which had $58 million remaining, into a two-year, $84 million deal last year. Stafford received a one-year extension for $55 million running through the 2027 season. Incentives make Stafford's extension worth up to $60 million.
A persistent pursuit of edge rusher Myles Garrett , which began in 2022, finally paid dividends in June. The Cleveland Browns dealt the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year to the Rams for a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, a 2029 third-round pick and edge rusher Jared Verse , who was 2024's NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year.
The Garrett acquisition had an unexpected major consequence. His addition inspired defensive tackle Aaron Donald , who was on track to be a first-ballot Hall of Famer in 2029, to unretire.
After winning the offseason, the Rams are heavy favorites to be Super Bowl LXI champions at 5-to-1, according to SportsLine. The Buffalo Bills have the next best odds at 10-to-1, followed by the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks.
The Rams assembled a team more reminiscent of a previous era before the salary cap was implemented in 1994. The NFL salary cap is $301.2 million for the 2026 league year. Each team's actual salary cap (known as adjusted salary cap) is typically different from the NFL's set amount because unused cap room can be carried over from one year to the next year and other adjustments can further increase or decrease cap space.
The Rams have an adjusted salary cap of $313.324 million. The league-wide average is $317.822 million according to NFLPA data. The New England Patriots have the NFL's highest adjusted salary cap at $352.979 million, largely thanks to carrying over $47.27 million of cap room, which is easily the most in the league. The Bills have the lowest at $301.58 million, which is only $380,000 above the league-wide number.
The Rams constructed a roster that is top-heavy, salary-cap-wise. Stafford has the 2026 largest cap number at $48,267,348. The only other 2026 cap number above $45 million belongs to Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert with $46.35 million.
Wide receiver Davante Adams and left tackle Alaric Jackson's Jackson have the 25th- and 35th-highest cap numbers in the NFL for 2026. Adams has the third-highest wide receiver figure at $28 million. Jackson's $25.4 million is fifth among offensive linemen (fourth for an offensive tackle).
Four other Rams have 2026 cap numbers that rank among the 10 highest at their respective positions. Kyren Williams , who signed a three-year, $33 million extension last July, has the third-biggest running back cap number at $11.7 million. Coleman Shelton's $9.5 million is fourth for a center. Kevin Dotson's $17.4 million is the seventh-largest offensive guard cap hit. Colby Parkinson has the ninth-highest tight end cap figure ($9.1 million).
The collective $48 million average yearly salary of McDuffie and Watson for the upgrade at cornerback is the NFL's second-highest, behind only the Indianapolis Colts tandem of Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward at $48.1 million. McDuffie's and Watson's combined $17.8 million 2026 cap hit is smaller than Ward's alone ($19.9 million). Their cap figures will jump significantly in 2027. McDuffie's will be a cornerback, high $30.8 million, while Watson's $22.7 million ranks 10th.
Garrett had five years worth $179 million remaining on his contract when acquired. His contract was almost immediately reworked. Instead of making $31.5 million in 2026, his salary was raised to $37 million, with $35.7 million converted into a signing bonus that would be prorated at $7.14 million annually against the salary cap from 2026 through 2030. His 2026 cap number is $8,840,680.
Garrett's 2027 compensation drops from $42.7 million to $32 million, while his 2028 money increases to $30 million from $24.8 million. His compensation for 2029 and 2030 remains at $40 million in each year.
There are two separate option bonuses, each for $15 million in 2027, to pick up dummy/voiding 2031 and 2032 contract years. Because this $30.145 million is being prorated on the salary cap from 2027 through 2031 at $6.029 million annually, Garrett's 2027 cap hit is $15.024 million. Given the market for elite pass rushers has changed dramatically since Garrett became the NFL's first $40 million per year non-quarterback in March 2025, it wouldn't be surprising for his deal to be renegotiated as early as next year.
The Rams had more than $15 million in existing cap space, according to NFLPA data, when Donald decided to come out of retirement on August 30. The Rams had retained his contractual rights when he retired after the 2023 season by placing him on the reserve/retired list. The remaining year left on his contract tolled or was frozen.
Because of some creative salary cap maneuvering when Donald retired in 2024, the Rams easily handled his contract upon reinstatement without anymore salary cap gymnastics. Donald's 2026 salary was just his league minimum $1.3 million before he and the Rams agreed on a one-year, $20 million deal worth a maximum of $30 million through incentives.
The $20 million is composed of a fully guaranteed $10 million base salary and $10 million in per-game roster bonuses, with $666,666.67 for each game on the 53-man roster, capped at 15 games. The $10 million in incentives is primarily tied to Donald's playtime and the Rams' postseason success. Donald gets $2.5 million if he has at least 15% of the defensive snaps in the regular season and the Rams make the playoffs. There's $1.25 million on the Rams' active roster for the wild card game or if a bye is earned for that playoff round. Being on the active roster for a divisional playoff game is worth another $1.25 million. Donald gets $2.5 million each for an NFC Championship Game win and a Super Bowl win, provided his regular-season defensive playtime reached 15% and he took at least 20% of the defensive snaps in the requisite game.
Technically, Donald is under contract for 2027 at his $1.345 million league minimum salary, and there are dummy/voiding 2028 through 2030 contract years. Donald has a $5.826 million 2026 cap number because his low 2027 salary triggered an obscure salary cap rule, the 50% Down Rule. Since Donald's second-year salary in 2027 is less than half of his first-year salary in 2026, the difference between the two salaries, including the $3.75 million of Donald's incentives classified as likely to be earned, is being treated as a signing bonus and prorated over these five years. As a result, Donald's 2026 cap number consists of $1.3 million categorized as base salary and $4.481 million as bonus proration. The $4.481 million of bonus proration applies to 2027 as well as each of the dummy/voiding 2028 through 2030 contract years.

title: 2027 NFL Draft predictions: Our experts pick No. 1 overall, biggest riser, strongest position and more
summary: A potentially loaded quarterback class garners significant attention, but the EDGE and WR groups should also be strong
full_text:
The 2027 NFL Draft is roughly eight months away, and a lot will change between now and then. Similar to a time capsule, CBS Sports' NFL Draft analysts answered questions fans may have as the college football and NFL seasons begin, with the intent of seeing how those responses age over the course of the season.
Ryan Wilson and I answer some of the draft's most pressing questions as we see them in early September.
Ryan Wilson : QB Dante Moore , Oregon . "Dante Moore is my QB1 heading into the 2026 season and the best bet to be the top pick next April because the tape already shows the traits of a No. 1 pick. Plus, he would've been the No. 2 pick in last spring's draft had he not returned to Oregon. He is composed, navigates the pocket naturally and can make the type of downfield throws that separate good college quarterbacks from future NFL starters . He still needs to be more consistent when the first read disappears or the pocket gets messy, but the best version of Moore looks like the best quarterback in this class."
Josh Edwards : QB Arch Manning , Texas . "Arch Manning does a good job operating within the pocket, and his last name obviously carries a lot of weight. If the decision between Oregon's Dante Moore, Manning or anyone else is remotely close, I could see an owner putting his thumb on the scale in favor of Manning. Manning could theoretically return for the 2027 season, but the odds are probably against it."
Wilson : Drew Mestemaker , Oklahoma State . "Drew Mestemaker went from a zero-star high school backup and North Texas walk-on to leading the country with 4,379 passing yards last season. He processes quickly, works through reads and throws with touch, although the arm strength is more solid than special. If that production follows him to Oklahoma State against better competition, the first-round conversation will get loud quickly."
Edwards : Kenny Minchey , Kentucky . "It is tough to pick an under-the-radar quarterback because quarterbacks transfer to receive more playing time. To fit the criteria, one would likely have to find a first-year starter in a system that fits him. Kenny Minchey lost the Notre Dame job to C.J. Carr last year and is now playing for Will Stein, who helped develop Dillon Gabriel and Dante Moore."
Wilson : OT Jordan Seaton , LSU . "Since we talked up Mestemaker above, we'll go with a non-QB here (though I would not be shocked if the answer does, in fact, end up being … Mestemaker). The move from Colorado to LSU gives left tackle Jordan Seaton an SEC stage to reinforce what the tape already shows. He has an enormous, thick frame but plays light on his feet, anchors against power and can wreak havoc in space. He also cut his pressures allowed from 37 in 2024 to seven last season. Stay healthy, and he could be the first offensive lineman drafted."
Edwards : WR Cam Coleman , Texas . " Auburn 's offense was really disjointed last season, so it is reasonable to think his play may improve with more reliable quarterback play. Through the offseason, Coleman's highlights have stuck with me as evidence of his potential."
Wilson : TE Trey'Dez Green , LSU . "LSU tight end Trey'Dez Green is already among the 10 best players on my preseason big board , but he has the physical profile to climb even higher. At 6-foot-7, he can line up inline, in the slot or outside, run away from linebackers and consistently create problems in the red zone. He caught seven touchdowns last season and set LSU's single-season record for a tight end while also showing legitimate blocking ability despite being listed at 238. Clean up the focus drops, and top-five buzz won't feel unreasonable."
Edwards : CB OJ Frederique Jr., Miami . "In watching Frederique this summer, he had some of the best man coverage skills of any cornerback I watched. He dealt with injuries last season, so it will be interesting to see how he rebounds. If healthy, he has the potential to be among the first cornerbacks drafted after Notre Dame's Leonard Moore ."
Wilson : QB, WR or EDGE . "It may be a three-way tie. Quarterback has Moore and Arch Manning at the top, with Julian Sayin , Jayden Maiava , Darian Mensah and the aforementioned Mestemaker just scratching the surface on that group . Wide receiver starts with Jeremiah Smith and Cam Coleman, while the edge group is headlined by Colin Simmons and Dylan Stewart . Each position currently has six players inside my top 50. QB will drive the conversation, but wide receiver and pass rusher may prove just as deep."
Edwards : WR . " Ohio State 's Jeremiah Smith and Texas' Cam Coleman are oft-mentioned premium talents in the 2027 class, but Indiana 's Charlie Becker is up there as well. Alabama 's Ryan Coleman-Williams has the potential to be one of those performers. The depth of the class continues well into Day 2. Defensive tackle could be up there as well if all the youth declares."
Wilson : IOL . "Interior offensive line looks like the weakest group right now. Greg Johnson is the top guard on my board at No. 30, followed by Kade Pieper at No. 46. That doesn't mean there won't be NFL starters in the group or that we won't have some current college tackles project to guard or center at the next level, but it will be something to monitor throughout the 2026 season."
Edwards : IOL . "In going through the summer scouting process, the sheer volume of interior offensive linemen is probably lower than at most other positions. The linebacker room may be relatively dependent on several young players entering the draft as opposed to returning to college football."
Wilson : Dolphins . "Miami is in a full reset with a new coach, an unproven starter in Malik Willis and a receiver room built around young players still finding their way. De'Von Achane is a bright spot, but no roster has a smaller margin for error. The Dolphins head into the season with 10 rookies listed as first- or second-teamers on the depth chart."
Edwards : Dolphins . "The roster is one of the worst I've seen in a long time. The intention of the season is to evaluate who may be part of the rebuild and what needs the franchise may have next offseason."
Wilson : Ohio State and the Bills . "Ohio State has the best player in college football in Jeremiah Smith, a QB in Julian Sayin who wins with patience and precision, and a defense that features Kenyatta Jackson, Jaylen McClain and tone-setting transfer Earl Little Jr .
"Is this finally the Bills' year? Because it sure feels like time is running out. Josh Allen is still in his prime and one of the best players in the league, and DJ Moore gives him the proven outside target he has been missing. Then there's a new (old) voice in Joe Brady, who is now the head coach, and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard should have the unit playing more aggressively and less predictably."
Edwards : Oregon and the Rams . "Oregon has the best returning roster, which was a pitfall in identifying Penn State as a contender last season. The Rams have the most talent of any one team. Can they stay healthy?"

title: Pro Football Hall of Fame makes massive voting changes after Bill Belichick snub: 7 things to know
summary: The elimination of the seniors category and reduction in the number of voters are among the biggest changes
full_text:
After Bill Belichick was snubbed from the Pro Football Hall of Fame during his first year as an eligible candidate last February, there were questions about whether the Hall needed to start thinking about changing its selection process , and that's exactly what has happened.
Hall of Fame president Jim Porter announced Friday that the HOF will make some massive changes to how players, coaches and contributors are selected.
"The Hall continually reviews its bylaws to ensure the selection process reflects the highest standards of integrity and the magnitude of election to the Pro Football Hall of Fame," Porter said in a statement. "There is no more important task at the Hall of Fame than the election of each new class."
The most notable change is probably the elimination of the seniors category. Another big change is that the selection committee will be trimmed from 50 members to just 28.
Here are the seven notable bylaw changes that will be implemented starting with the Class of 2027:
1. Committee size: The selection committee will be reduced from 50 members to 28. Their voting status (25 voting, three nonvoting participants) will be determined annually. The slate of selectors will be announced after all 50 individuals who elected the Class of 2026 are notified of their status.
2. Committee structure: Under the old structure, there was one voter representing each NFL team (32 total), 17 at-large selectors and one Pro Football Writers of America representative. Under the new structure, there will be 27 at-large selectors and one PFWA representative.
3. Player eligibility: The seniors category will essentially be eliminated, with everyone now going into a single pool of all eligible candidates following the mandatory five-year retirement period.
4. Contributor eligibility: This will expand from individuals who "contributed to the game outside of playing or coaching" to consideration of a candidate's full football résumé, which may include playing, coaching and other contributions to the sport.
5. Candidates considered at annual meeting: When the committee votes on the finalists in each class, it will consider 15 people: 13 players, one coach and one contributor. The coach and contributor will be determined by their respective subcommittees. Under the old bylaws, the finalists were whittled down to 15 modern-era players, three seniors, one coach and one contributor for a total of 20.
6. Seniors on final ballot: With the seniors category eliminated, senior players will no longer be given a special spot on the final ballot. The new bylaws will eliminate the previous maximum of three senior finalists, with all eligible players now considered together in a single pool regardless of how long they have been retired.
7. Carryover candidates: Under the old rule, if a player was a finalist for the Hall of Fame, he would automatically return as a finalist the following year, but that will no longer be the case.
One other notable change is that only one person will present each finalist for induction, and that person won't be part of the selection committee. Under the old rule, a player would usually be presented by the selection committee member who represented the team the player played for. So Drew Brees, who was inducted in 2026, would have had his case presented by the committee member representing the Saints .
According to Porter, the Hall is making these massive changes to help overcome "unintended biases" in three main areas: "The disparate skills of the individuals making the initial presentations of nominees for election at the annual meeting; the assignment of a selector to each of the NFL 's 32 member clubs; and issues related to players reaching their final years of eligibility in the modern-era players category."
In Belichick's situation, he was under consideration last year with one contributor (Robert Kraft) and three seniors. To get in, Belichick would have needed 80% of the vote from the 50-person committee, but that didn't happen. For the upcoming year, if he's a finalist again, he'll go up against one contributor and 13 players. Each class going forward will have between three and seven members, so almost 50% of the finalists could be enshrined each year if the vote goes their way.
This is a massive set of changes by the Hall of Fame, and it probably hurts senior candidates the most. Under the old rules, they would be named finalists in their own separate category, but under the new rules, they'll be lumped in with all eligible players, and it's hard to see very many of them getting enshrined going forward.
The new selection process will be put to the test for the first time in 2027, when we'll see several first-time eligible players like Ben Roethlisberger , Rob Gronkowski and Adrian Peterson .
