title: Unjust: Football Hall of Fame voting change likely closes door on Browns Clay Matthews Jr.
summary: What it takes to become a Pro Football Hall of Famer is not written in stone. Stats, impact, accolades, team accomplishments, and more tend to lead voters to give certain players a lot more attention than others. For Cleveland Browns LB Clay Matthews Jr., that process has moved his name forward but never into the […]
full_text: Sep 22, 2019; Cleveland, OH, USA; Cleveland Browns former player Clay Matthews Jr. (57) as he is inducted into the Browns Ring of Honor during the halftime show against the Los Angeles Rams at FirstEnergy Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports What it takes to become a Pro Football Hall of Famer is not written in stone. Stats, impact, accolades, team accomplishments, and more tend to lead voters to give certain players a lot more attention than others. For Cleveland Browns LB Clay Matthews Jr. , that process has moved his name forward but never into the winner’s circle for a Gold Jacket and an iconic bust. For those who don’t know Matthews’ story, you might know his son, Clay Matthews III , from his excellent career with the Green Bay Packers. Matthews 19-year playing career once again saw him advance in the Hall of Fame process for seniors heading into this year’s induction, but he once again fell short. During 16 years with the Browns and three with the Atlanta Falcons, Matthews compiled 82.5 sacks, just under 1,600 tackles, 16 interceptions, 24 forced fumbles, 29 fumble recoveries, and two defensive touchdowns. According to Pro-Football-Reference’s Approximate Value , Matthews is the 104th-best player since 1960, and one of the few eligible retirees that high on the list without a bust in Canton, Ohio. Clay’s daughter Jennifer has continually pounded the table for her father to receive his rightful induction: Pops made it to the next round of the @ProFootballHOF Class of 2025 & I’ll continue to champion this amazing,humble man & his unreal record-setting career, including him having the most games played by an LB in NFL history. 19 yrs at linebacker is an anomaly. #ClayMatthewsHOF pic.twitter.com/tJr6mgCK45 — Jennifer Matthews (@JennMatthews57) October 4, 2024 Sadly, after the Hall of Fame made changes to their voting process on Friday, Matthews and other senior candidates may have seen their chances of joining the immortals vanish. As noted via ESPN : All players will now be considered in one pool rather than split into either “modern era” or “seniors,” with the latter being players who had had their modern era eligibility expire after 25 years. Players will still be eligible for induction five years after their retirement but will simply remain on the list of all eligible players after that. How does that impact Matthews and the rest of what used to be the senior candidates ? Previously, a maximum of three seniors could be included on the ballot of finalists. Players also no longer graduate to the seniors category after a number of years, meaning all player designees remain in the same pool. Now, Matthews will no longer just be contending with players from his own era, which he has continually lost out to (unfairly, according to anyone who loves the Browns). Instead, anyone and everyone who gets on the ballot gets to stay on the ballot, further cluttering the chances that a player passed over, over and over again, will suddenly get enough votes, even if they deserve it. Do you believe that Clay Matthews Jr. deserves to be in the Hall of Fame? What do you think about these new rules that will help more modern players get inducted each year but limit players who retired before the 2000 season? Join the conversation! title: Browns DT Mike Hall squashes dustup with fellow Buckeye, RB Quinshon Judkins
summary: The Cleveland Browns spent the early part of this week deciding which players to retain on this year’s initial 53-man roster. Then, the coaching staff and front office made decisions regarding the practice squad roster. Now, it is time to spend time getting this new offense down and figuring out the wrinkles that need to […]
full_text: BEREA, OH - AUGUST 05: Defensive Tackle Mike Hall Jr. #51 of the Cleveland Browns practices drills during Training Camp at their CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on August 5, 2024 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns spent the early part of this week deciding which players to retain on this year’s initial 53-man roster . Then, the coaching staff and front office made decisions regarding the practice squad roster . Now, it is time to spend time getting this new offense down and figuring out the wrinkles that need to be fixed, with the players getting a few days off . Defensive tackle Mike Hall had spent part of training camp with an injury. A couple of fans and media outlets had wondered if he would be released or traded this year due to various injuries and lackluster production so far in his NFL career. Hall missed 10 practices with what the front office described as “an undisclosed injury.” And while we don’t know what the injury is exactly, we do know how he became injured and what caused it. In a practice session in shorts and lids on August 1, Hall was slotted at right defensive tackle. The snap to QB Deshaun Watson came as usual in the shotgun formation, and Hall was rushing and became engaged with LG Zion Johnson. All of a sudden, Hall stopped his progress, lowered his head, and bent over. Next, RB Quinshon Judkins came from the backfield and leveled Hall, who wasn’t even looking anymore. Judkins pushed Hall with both hands as the DT crashed to the turf. Then Judkins flared out to the left flats as an exit route option. What appeared to have occurred initially was that Johnson’s left hand must have struck Hall in the neck/throat area when he was reaching out to slow down his defender. That is when Hall started to buckle and lower his head but remained upright. As Judkins was coming out of the backfield, all he saw was a free man rushing into his gap, and he did what running backs do: block. #Browns training camp practice was a little intense today. pic.twitter.com/QmpT1WRetg — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) August 1, 2026 Hall was down for the count. He left the field for a bit, came back for a few plays, and then was back in team drills later in the non-padded practice. Next, he missed 10 practices. Looked like Mike got hurt on this play? He clearly stopped before Q laid him out — Leroy Brown (@LeroyTheBrown) August 1, 2026 Rumors have spread that Hall and Judkins were involved in some kind of altercation in the locker room after that practice. That has not been substantiated, of course; that could be just others spreading the rumor. Hall did finally come out with a statement after the September 2 practice. He stated regarding the dust-up with his former Ohio State teammate: “Yeah, I mean, we’re teammates at the end of the day, so, I mean, it’s just a little, you know, mishap on the field.” Then another reporter asked about the locker room scenario: “Like I said before, he’s my teammate, so I mean, got to talk to him at some time. But we’re getting ready for Jacksonville, and that’s all I’m worried about.” Apparently, if there is any ill will, Hall seems to be over it. And hopefully, someone has tutored Judkins to save those crushing blocks for Cleveland’s opponents. A player like Hall is expected to play a significant role in the middle of the defensive line this season for the Browns. Given the team’s lack of depth off the edge, Hall may also see some time there as well.

full_text: May 8, 2026; Berea, OH, USA; Cleveland Browns managing and principal partner Jimmy Haslam, right, talks to executive vice president, football operations & general manager Andrew Berry during rookie minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cleveland Browns salary cap has been the topic of conversation since the team traded for and signed QB Deshaun Watson to the ridiculous fully guaranteed contract . There were concerns when the deal went down; those have only multiplied with his poor performance on the field . There is still some public uncertainty about how much insurance relief Cleveland will get from Watson’s contract due to injuries , but GM Andrew Berry has money to work with this year and moving forward despite a huge amount of dead cap space (following the trade of Myles Garrett and Joel Bitonio’s retirement ). Jared Verse , Garrett’s replacement, will only cost the team a total of $5 million total over the next two seasons , which helps the salary cap greatly. Now that the Browns, along with the rest of the NFL, have made all the big moves to get to their initial 53-man roster , Over the Cap has adjusted its salary cap figures for each team in the league . According to OTC, Cleveland has $14.7 million in cap space to use in 2026, good for 12th in the NFL and the most among AFC North teams. Their numbers show that six teams are still over the cap and need to restructure some contracts, which we’ve seen happening, at least reportedly, over the last 24 hours For next offseason, as of now, the Browns have the 11th most cap space with $58 million available, again most in the division, with the Baltimore Ravens at the bottom of the league with a whopping $41 million over the projected salary cap. Over the Cap projects another big jump in the salary cap next year, up another $26 million from this year’s cap. While a myriad of things will change by 2028, OTC has Cleveland near the bottom of the league that season with “just” $67 million in cap space. The Buffalo Bills ($16 million) and the San Francisco 49ers (negative $13 million) are at the bottom of the available space three seasons away. title: Quinnen Williams sees growth in the Cowboys defense
summary: Quinnen Williams arrived in Dallas halfway through a defensive disaster, but his seven games in Dallas did little to change the trajectory of a defense that had already gone badly off the rails. Nine months later, Williams sees something very different. “The growth, it’s like night and day,” Williams said of the strides made by […]
full_text: Quinnen Williams arrived in Dallas halfway through a defensive disaster, but his seven games in Dallas did little to change the trajectory of a defense that had already gone badly off the rails. Nine months later, Williams sees something very different . “The growth, it’s like night and day,” Williams said of the strides made by the Cowboys on the defensive side of the ball, and in such a short period of time. “Starting in OTAs, and starting the first week of training camp, getting a chance to go against one of the best offenses in battle every single day has helped us tremendously. The mindset coming from the coaches, top down to the players and to the leadership, has been drastically changed. It’s just fun, man.” “It’s been amazing — from where we started off in OTAs to where we are at now,” he explained. “We’ve got some fine tuning, some things to clean up, some things to do, but I feel comfortable. The progressions that we made, the growth and the development that we have made, and to go into the right direction that we wanted to go into.” There are several reasons for that change. The Cowboys brought in Christian Parker and a modernized defensive scheme. They also surrounded the new coordinator with considerably more talent, trading for Rashan Gary and Dee Winters, acquiring Jalen Thompson, Cobie Durant, P.J. Locke, and Von Miller in free agency, and added talent via the draft with the likes of Caleb Downs, Malachi Lawrence, and Jaishawn Barham. And then there is the daily competition. Williams compared the experience to his time at Alabama, when he was constantly going against future first-round picks. Only now, he says, the competition is even better. “The last time I kind of felt this was when I was at ‘Bama, when it came down to you going against first-rounders across from you,” he said. “But here in the NFL, it’s All-Pros everywhere, getting a chance to go against one of the best offenses in the league and one of the best quarterbacks in the league. “And we’ve got one of the best offensive lines in the league, so using them as a helping tool to get better every single day, and the urgency level from a defensive standpoint to get better every single day. It’s been well-needed and fun. It’s definitely a battle.” A new defensive coordinator, a revamped roster, and an elite offense providing daily competition. Williams sees the difference. But notice what he doesn’t say. He doesn’t say the Cowboys have arrived. He doesn’t say the defense is fixed. He doesn’t even say they’re good. Instead, he says: “I just can’t wait to see the process and the results from all the hard work, but we’re not done yet.” That’s probably the most important part of everything Williams had to say. The pieces are in place. Whether they fit together remains to be seen. We’ll find out more in the season opener against the Giants.

full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Von Miller #40 of the Dallas Cowboys walks off the field after the 2026 NFL preseason game against the New Orleans Saints at AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images Von Miller was a big addition to the Cowboys during the offseason, and he couldn’t be happier to be back in Texas. Tyler Guyton is entering the most important season of his young career, and his play, or lack thereof, will have a lot to do with how Dallas performs on offense. Joe Milton was brought back on the practice squad, and according to Dak Prescott, it gives the quarterback room a boost. Camden Brown has taken full advantage of his opportunities, but his main impact this year likely won’t be as a wide receiver. Von Miller on looming debut for the Cowboys: ‘My smile is back’ – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Von Miller has been in the NFL for a decade and a half and has had tremendous success. However, being back in Texas and playing for the Cowboys is something that means a lot to him. “[The media is] probably the 50th person to tell me that,” said the eight-time Pro Bowler. “The smile has come back, you know? I’ve always loved playing football. I’ve been able to play for some amazing teams, with amazing quarterbacks and amazing coaches. But it’s just something different about being here. … Coming here to The Star and seeing this amazing facility, and going to the stadium, I am glad we had that preseason game because I was in awe.” Why did the Dallas Cowboys choose Sam Howell over Joe Milton III? – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Joe Milton is back in Dallas on their practice squad after losing the QB2 battle to Sam Howell. However, the reason the latter won out isn’t too surprising. One of the more debated topics of the roster moves around the NFL over the past week was the Dallas Cowboys’ decision to waive backup quarterback Joe Milton III in favor of keeping Sam Howell on the 53-man roster to be the primary backup to Dak Prescott. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer explained that the decision to keep two quarterbacks was likely always going to be the case to preserve roster spots at other positions. While three quarterbacks made the initial 53-man roster , Milton was waived a day later to make room for running back Emari Demercado . Cowboys add veteran tight end to practice squad – Connor Livesay, Blogging The Boys The Cowboys have being a lot of wheeling and dealing lately. On Thursday, they added veteran tight end James Mitchell. After a nail-biting 24 hours waiting to see if quarterback Joe Milton would clear waivers and return to the practice squad, the Dallas Cowboys are not done adding to it. The team announced late on Thursday that they have signed veteran tight end James Mitchell to their practice squad. Mitchell started his career in Detroit after being selected in the fifth round of the 2022 NFL Draft out of Virginia Tech. 2026 NFL season X factors: Key players for all 32 teams – Ben Solak, ESPN There’s a lot of buzz about the Cowboys offense going into this season, especially with George Pickens being back. However, Tyler Guyton is the pivotal piece. Guyton has the physical tools of a quality starting left tackle, but he has suffered mental lapses and taken easy penalties. Since he entered the league in 2024, Guyton is third among tackles in penalties per game (0.84). He has missed time because of ankle, shoulder and knee injuries. Now, he needs to string together consistent, mistake-free play. A leap from Guyton would benefit the entire offensive line. Guyton and right tackle Terence Steele warrant some chip help in pass protection, but it’s hard to cater to both sides of the line. Dak Prescott Shares What Joe Milton Return Means To Cowboys – Randy Gurzi, SI.com Dak Prescott has built a relationship with Joe Milton since he came to Dallas in a trade last year. Now that he’s back on the practice squad, Prescott expressed what having him back means. “It means a lot. Just me, personally, I thought he would’ve been picked up in the waivers or whatever it is. Fortunate for us, we got a hell of a player back and a guy that makes our room better, a guy that makes our team better. His spirit, just the way that he approaches the day, he’s a hell of a dude, he’s a hell of a competitor, one of the best at throwing the ball, honestly, and just his talent. Just the way he’s jumped and progressed from year to year, I know what’s ahead of him,” Prescott said via Jon Machota of The Athletic . Mailbag: How much will Brown contribute? – Nick Eatman, DallasCowboys.com Wide receiver Camden Brown has been a fan favorite during training camp and the preseason, and people were ecstatic that he made the final roster. However, the expectations for him need to be realistic. Now, if he shows the ability to play well on special teams and he’s valuable enough to take to the game and maybe play a little on offense, then let’s see it. But my guess is that he’ll probably be inactive for a lot of this season. And there’s nothing wrong with that. I saw Miles Austin sit for a few years before finally making a huge splash in Year 4. And think about Ryan Flournoy was barely a factor for two years and now he’s WR3 who won’t play much special teams at all. Daily discussion question: What is your biggest concern for the Giants game?

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 9
summary: It is Day 9 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - JANUARY 17: Running back Emmitt Smith #22 of the Dallas Cowboys runs against the San Francisco 49ers in the 1992 NFC Championship Game at Candlestick Park on January 17, 1993 in San Francisco, California. The Cowboys defeated the 49ers 30-20. (Photo by James Smith/Getty Images) It is Day 9 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We’re down to single digits now as we hit Day 9 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff and we go back to the heavyweight NFC Championship victory that kept the Cowboys on course for back-to-back Super Bowl titles. The Cowboys had won at Candlestick Park the previous year, then dominated the rematch at home during a magic season. Sunday, January 23, 1994 Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 38, San Francisco 49ers 21 There was no shortage of confidence for this game. Dallas had beaten San Francisco twice in the previous 12 months, including a 26-17 regular-season victory, and Jimmy Johnson publicly guaranteed another win in the days leading up to the championship game. The 49ers arrived after crushing the Giants in the Divisional Round, but the defending champions immediately demonstrated who still controlled the NFC. Dallas opened the game with an impressive 75-yard drive, marching down the field in 11 plays before Emmitt Smith finished it with a five-yard touchdown run. San Francisco answered early in the second quarter when Steve Young connected with Tom Rathman for a seven-yard score to tie the game at 7-7. From there, though, the Cowboys began to take complete control. Daryl Johnston put Dallas back in front with a four-yard touchdown run before the defense delivered the next big moment. John Taylor deflected a Young pass into the hands of Thomas Everett, who returned the interception deep into San Francisco territory. Troy Aikman quickly made the turnover count, finding Smith for an 11-yard touchdown that extended the Cowboys’ lead to 21-7. Dallas added another touchdown before the break, with Aikman finishing a 72-yard drive by connecting with Jay Novacek from 19 yards out. That sent the Cowboys into halftime with a commanding 28-7 advantage. Dallas had reached the end zone on four of its first five possessions while piling up 273 total yards and 19 first downs in a dominant opening half. The biggest concern arrived early in the third quarter when Aikman suffered a severe concussion after defensive lineman Dennis Brown’s knee struck his helmet. Aikman eventually left the game and was later taken to hospital. He finished 14-of-18 for 177 yards and two touchdowns, and years later said he still had no memory of playing in the game. San Francisco attempted to take advantage, with Ricky Watters scoring from four yards to reduce the deficit to 28-14. Backup quarterback Bernie Kosar responded exactly as Dallas needed. He led an 82-yard possession and connected with Alvin Harper for a 42-yard touchdown, restoring a three-score lead and crushing the 49ers’ hopes of a comeback. Eddie Murray added a 50-yard field goal in the fourth quarter to make it 38-14. Young scored on a one-yard run with 4:06 remaining, but by then the NFC Championship had already been decided. Dallas had beaten its greatest conference rival for a second consecutive postseason. This game belongs on the countdown because it confirmed that the Cowboys’ first championship was no one-year wonder. San Francisco remained one of the most talented teams in football, yet Dallas had now beaten them in consecutive NFC Championship Games. Even losing Aikman could not derail a roster deep enough to finish the job. #Cowboys vs #49ers 1993 NFC Championship Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 38, San Francisco 49ers 21 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/abZj7qW3aW — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 4, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Kosar produced a 123.8 passer rating in relief, completing five of nine passes for 83 yards and the crucial touchdown to Harper. title: 3 players the Cowboys could extend during the 2026 season
summary: It is not usual for the Dallas Cowboys to announce a contract extension for a player during the regular season. But let’s pretend they might and look at three key contributors the Cowboys could look to extend early before they are able to hit free agency. Brevyn Spann-Ford One of the more interesting players on […]
full_text: Sep 21, 2025; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Dallas Cowboys tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford (89) runs after a catch against the Chicago Bears during the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It is not usual for the Dallas Cowboys to announce a contract extension for a player during the regular season. But let’s pretend they might and look at three key contributors the Cowboys could look to extend early before they are able to hit free agency. Brevyn Spann-Ford One of the more interesting players on this 2026 roster is tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford. Spann-Ford has taken ahold of the TE2 job with force. While starter Jake Ferguson had a very good camp and solidified himself as the top tight end on the team, Spann-Ford proved he deserves to stay in Dallas for quite some time. Spann-Ford signed a three-year deal with the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent after the 2024 NFL draft. He will be a restricted free agent after the 2026 season, and while the Cowboys are likely able to keep him for relatively cheap in 2027, his limited play in 2025 and the development he showed during this year’s training camp show he deserves long-term security. Spann-Ford will not demand market-setting money on a contract and his ability as a blocker and receiver is needed in the Cowboys offense. The Cowboys would be wise to get ahead of this deal and lock in Spann-Ford long-term with a team-friendly deal. Ryan Flournoy Similar to Brevyn Spann-Ford, Ryan Flournoy will be a restricted free agent in 2027. With what he showed in 2025 and what we’re all expecting him to show in 2026, the Cowboys should seriously consider paying Flournoy now instead of risking him on a tender and paying him a significant guaranteed salary. With the uncertainty surrounding George Pickens future in Dallas, locking up Ryan Flournoy long-term would be a great move to give the Cowboys a high-upside receiver in the room if Pickens is to leave due to his market at the end of the 2026 season. Otito Ogbonnia While Otito Ogbonnia may not be one of the sexier additions to this Cowboys defense, he will play a pivotal role on the Cowboys defense in 2026. Ogbonnia has yet to prove himself as a starter on the defensive line in his four-year career, but Christian Parker and the Cowboys defensive coaching staff view him just as that. Ogbonnia had a very nice training camp as a starting defensive end in base looks, and earned a ballcap in preseason games with a majority of the Cowboys starters on defense. Ogbonnia signed a one-year, $2.75-million dollar contract with the Cowboys this offseason, but with him already solidifying a starting spot, that contract seems like a steal for the Cowboys. Ogbonnia won’t be a guy to register double-digit sacks, but his ability to impact the running game and his position versatility is much needed in Christian Parker’s defense. Locking up Ogbonnia with a team-friendly two-year extension would keep him in Dallas through 2029 season, and his position versatility would be a fit with any scheme used in the foreseeable future.

title: Dallas Cowboys 2026 predictions: Studs and duds on the roster
summary: With the Cowboys trimmed to 53 players and their practice squad finalized, the roster’s overall depth looks stronger than it has in recent years. Last season’s weaknesses have largely turned into strengths, positioning the team for a legitimate push back into the postseason. Optimism peaks at this time of year as key contributors prepare for […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 23: Tyler Guyton #60 of the Dallas Cowboys lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the Cowboys trimmed to 53 players and their practice squad finalized, the roster’s overall depth looks stronger than it has in recent years. Last season’s weaknesses have largely turned into strengths, positioning the team for a legitimate push back into the postseason. Optimism peaks at this time of year as key contributors prepare for the opener. Still, every season brings surprises—breakout performers who exceed expectations and others who fall short. Here are the players primed to emerge as welcome additions in 2026 and those most likely to regress. Duds Jake Ferguson Ferguson opened the 2025 season on a tear, averaging eight receptions across the first five games. That production faded sharply afterward, and he never regained the same rhythm. Don’t expect a return to those early numbers. The Cowboys’ offense simply has too many high-priority targets for Ferguson to command a consistent share. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens headline the receiving corps, while Ryan Flournoy is poised for an expanded role. Brevyn Spann-Ford is also earning more snaps as a blocker and could see additional targets in two-tight-end packages. Ferguson is unlikely to approach his career-high reception total from last season. Compounding the issue is limited explosiveness after the catch—he posted his lowest yards-after-catch figure despite a relatively strong average depth of target. Limited opportunity and diminished playmaking after the catch make Ferguson a candidate for disappointment in Dallas. The right tackle position Credit the Cowboys for addressing right tackle proactively. Last week they acquired former first-round pick Broderick Jones from the Pittsburgh Steelers, with Coach Schottenheimer stating that Jones will compete directly with Terence Steele. Competition can elevate performance, yet both players have shown significant limitations recently. Steele has struggled in pass protection the past two seasons, particularly against speed rushers. Jones, meanwhile, ranked 80th out of 89 qualifying tackles in run blocking according to PFF. Neither option inspires confidence. The Cowboys will need to manage what looks like a challenging situation at the position. Conor Riley has significant work ahead. Camden Brown Put the pitchforks down. As impressive as Camden Brown was in earning a roster spot, a meaningful role in 2026 remains unrealistic. Consider Ryan Flournoy’s solid but modest 35-reception season as the team’s third receiver last year. On game days, Lamb, Pickens, Flournoy, and KaVontae Turpin will occupy the active roster when healthy. Jonathan Mingo also brings greater special-teams value and reliable receiving contributions. Brown would need to prove himself against starting-caliber defenders rather than camp competition fighting for the final roster spots. He remains a worthwhile developmental piece for the future, but he is far from ready for anything approaching a supporting role this season. Studs Jaishawn Barham The Cowboys’ 2026 draft class offers genuine excitement, with Caleb Downs expected to make an immediate impact. Jaishawn Barham, however, is positioned for a strong rookie contribution within Christian Parker’s defense. He will not start right away, and that is fine. When he sees the field, his power and athleticism will strengthen the run defense as he consistently defeats blockers at the line of scrimmage. Barham also displays sharp instincts, frequently finding himself in the right place at the right time. Expect him to carve out a productive rotational role at linebacker and post solid statistical production. The Cowboys will challenge the former Michigan standout, and he is ready to respond. Tyler Guyton Bet on Tyler Guyton’s third-year leap. Once informed he would compete for the starting left tackle job, Guyton quickly separated himself from Nathan Thomas and locked down the position early in camp. Thomas was later traded to Houston, leaving Guyton free to develop without looking over his shoulder. Now healthy, his technique has improved steadily throughout the offseason. He held up well against the Los Angeles Rams’ talented front during joint practices. With his draft pedigree and the high standards expected of Cowboys offensive linemen, a strong season could rapidly elevate Guyton’s trajectory and put him in Pro Bowl conversations. Shavon Revel Jr. Like Guyton, Shavon Revel enters the year healthier and further removed from his knee injury. His rough rookie season is behind him, and the arrival of defensive coordinator Christian Parker should accelerate his growth. Parker has a strong record of developing cornerbacks, and Revel’s size and athletic profile fit the scheme well. Early signs are encouraging—Revel has already performed solidly in matchups against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Although he is not currently listed as a starter, DaRon Bland’s history of inconsistent availability makes it likely Revel will see starting snaps. His continued improvement could shape the secondary’s overall performance this season.

title: Cowboys add veteran tight end to practice squad
summary: After a nail-biting 24 hours waiting to see if quarterback Joe Milton would clear waivers and return to the practice squad, the Dallas Cowboys are not done adding to it. The team announced late on Thursday that they have signed veteran tight end James Mitchell to their practice squad. Mitchell started his career in Detroit […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - AUGUST 28: James Mitchell #85 of the Carolina Panthers runs the ball during the second half of a preseason game against the Houston Texans at Bank of America Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a nail-biting 24 hours waiting to see if quarterback Joe Milton would clear waivers and return to the practice squad, the Dallas Cowboys are not done adding to it. The team announced late on Thursday that they have signed veteran tight end James Mitchell to their practice squad. Mitchell started his career in Detroit after being selected in the fifth round of the 2022 NFL Draft out of Virginia Tech. Mitchell is a good veteran option to have with NFL experience, and the ability to impact the game as a receiver and blocker if one of the top three tight ends miss time. In his three years in the NFL, Mitchell has hauled in just 16 receptions for 169 yards and one touchdown. He has played in 35 NFL games with one start, most of that with the Detroit Lions. He was most recently in the Carolina Panthers training camp. Despite his lack of production, Mitchell was viewed as a mid-round tight end by many during the 2022 NFL draft cycle. The Cowboys waived Mitch Van Voreen in the corresponding move to create space for Mitchell. Don’t expect Mitchell to make much if any impact in 2026 unless injuries strike, but the Cowboys continue to make smart moves by churning the bottom of the roster and making sure their practice squad has “NFL ready” players on it in case of an emergency. They can also start developing them for more in 2027.

title: One outlet has extreme confidence in Dallas against the Giants
summary: Bucky Brooks of NFL.com believes the Dallas Cowboys are true Super Bowl contenders this season. And Jerry Jones, head cheerleader for the Dallas Cowboys, is confident the Cowboys can compete for a Super Bowl in 2026. “I feel like we’ve got a chance to really be good,” Jones said. “It’s going to be hard… Bottom […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Brian Burns #0 of the New York Giants and Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys interact during the game at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The New York Giants won 34-17. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bucky Brooks of NFL.com believes the Dallas Cowboys are true Super Bowl contenders this season. And Jerry Jones, head cheerleader for the Dallas Cowboys, is confident the Cowboys can compete for a Super Bowl in 2026. “I feel like we’ve got a chance to really be good,” Jones said. “It’s going to be hard… Bottom line is, I love the excitement. [The media], for all practical purposes, don’t expect us to be a contender in the Super Bowl. Y’all don’t. Why would you? I like that, I do. I like that, and I like what we’ve put together to show you that we can do it.” The Cowboys hype has even prompted Adam Schefter to issue a warning to Stephen A. Smith . I got some bad news for Stephen A. Smith: The Dallas Cowboys are coming. They are coming this year and Stephen A. is gonna be tested. I’m telling you right now, it’s gonna be a long, anxious, nervous year for Stephen A. Smith. Be ready. Be that as it may, the Super Bowl is still far away, but the journey starts in Week 1. And for the season opener, the Cowboys are clear favorites against the Giants, at least according to NFL.com. All but one of their 10 panelists are projecting the Cowboys to win their season opener . Cowboys-Giants predictions are in. Football is so back! pic.twitter.com/8T1JmZpHsz — SleeperCowboys (@SleeperCowboys) September 2, 2026 Expectations are high for Dallas, and not just for the season opener. NFL.com gathered 19 of their analysts to predict this year’s division winners , and they have the Cowboys taking the NFC East. NFC EAST CHAMPS: Dallas Cowboys 1) Dallas Cowboys | 12 votes: Abdoo, Bergman, Ely, Filice, Gordon, Kownack, Okada, Patra, Shook, Smith, Umerani, Yam. 2) Philadelphia Eagles | 7 votes: Band, Cersosimo, McWilliams, Parr, Reuter, Rosenthal, Zierlein. Hype is never hard to find with the Cowboys, but this offseason has been different. They’ve been relatively drama-free , all the while making it clear a Super Bowl is the goal and they’re not shying away from it. So, why not the NFC East? The defense has been overhauled — including the addition of a Defensive Rookie of the Year front-runner in Caleb Downs and defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Dak Prescott’s offense is loaded and healthy and has finished as a top-five scorer in four of the past five seasons. Dallas is coming off back-to-back seven-win seasons. The last time Dallas had consecutive non-winning campaigns, it went 12-5 the following year and won the division in Mike McCarthy’s second year at the helm. Brian Schottenheimer is in Year 2 and has Texas-sized aspirations. Dan Parr, also of NFL.com, predicts the Cowboys will again have a top 5 offense this year. This is standard territory for the Cowboys. They have finished among the top five teams in OPPG in four of the past five seasons, with Dak Prescott ’s injury-shortened 2024 campaign the lone deviation. Prescott seems to still be in his prime after ranking among the top five quarterbacks in QBR and passing EPA last season. Dallas boasts the game’s top wide receiver duo, with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens performing at an All-Pro level. RB Javonte Williams kicked the injury bug that bit him earlier in his career and broke out in his first year in Big D, ranking ninth in the league with 1,201 rushing yards. If there’s one potentially fatal flaw, it’s at offensive tackle, with Dallas trading for Steelers castoff Broderick Jones , who is coming off a neck injury, in an attempt to shore things up at the position before the season begins . Barring pass protection on the edges becoming a thorn in its side, Brian Schottenheimer’s crew should be slicing through defenses again. And the defense? That’s where the optimism gets a little more complicated. The Athletic’s Mike Sando spoke with six NFL executives about their rankings of the top NFC teams, and wonders how much can the defense improve? “Anything is better than what they did last year on defense,” the voter placing Dallas second in the NFC said. “They shocked the system by trading Micah Parsons, and I just think generally speaking, new coordinators on defense create variance.” The voter ranking Dallas fifth thought the Cowboys’ defense might outrank the Packers’ defense, notable in light of the Parsons trade last year. “I like the coordinator,” this voter said of Parker. “He is going to help maximize what they have. The secondary is still not a strength, but they have an impressive front seven.” “Quinnen Williams is good, and they have a little more girth up front, so it should be better, but they’ve got some unknowns there too with coaches and philosophy,” the voter ranking Dallas eighth said. “I have defensive concerns, for sure,” one said. “Do they have enough pass rush? How healthy is Overshown? How good are the corners? But they did address the interior with Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark, and I like Caleb Downs. They will be better up the middle.” But everything starts in Week 1. A convincing win against the Giants would be a good first step toward validating all this optimism. And while the offense is expected to carry its share of the load, all eyes will be on the defense. Can Christian Parker’s unit improve just enough to turn the Cowboys from an intriguing team into a true contender?

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Sources: Cowboys restructure deals of Clark, Bland, Ferguson – Todd Archer, ESPN Could more personnel moves be on the horizon for Dallas? The Dallas Cowboys created a little more than $19 million in salary cap space by restructuring the contracts of three players, sources told ESPN. Veteran defensive tackle Kenny Clark , cornerback DaRon Bland and tight end Jake Ferguson had their deals reworked to give the Cowboys flexibility as the 2026 season begins or allow the club to carry over any unused space to 2027. According to the NFL Players Association website, the Cowboys had roughly $14.2 million of cap space before the restructured contracts. Cowboys QB Dak Prescott, three others selected captains for 2026 season – Joseph Hoyt, The Dallas Morning News The Cowboys have named their 2026 captains. A bit different approach and some new faces will lead the Cowboys in 2026. The Cowboys have an 11-person leadership council for this year’s team. Now they have a smaller group of captains to go with it. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced the team’s four captains Thursday. Quarterback Dak Prescott was the lone offensive captain. He’s joined by defensive tackles Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark, as well as kicker Brandon Aubrey. Dak Prescott on Joe Milton’s return, ‘focused’ offseason & more – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys were thrilled to have Joe Milton clear waivers and return to the practice squad. Starting QB Dak Prescott speaks on that and more with Tommy Yarrish. FRISCO, Texas – It’s been a busy week for the Dallas Cowboys as they wrap up training camp and prepare for the regular season. First comes a league mandated break, where Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott said he’d enjoy some time with his daughters but find a way to get his heart rate going. Dallas’ quarterback room is now back at three, after the team brought Joe Milton back on the practice squad Wednesday afternoon. Prescott is glad that he’s back. “It means a lot,” Prescott said of Milton’s return. “Obviously, me just personally, I thought he would’ve gotten picked up in the waivers. Fortunate for us, we got a hell of a player back and a guy that makes our room better, a guy that makes our team better. His spirit, just the way that he approaches the day… he’s a hell of a dude, a hell of a competitor.” Cowboys have complete confidence in Tyler Guyton at left tackle – Brandon Loree, Blogging the Boys No one had more questions coming into training camp than left tackle Tyler Guyton. With just a few days left before the regular season, the Cowboys seem to have a ton of confidence in their starting left tackle. One of the offseason’s biggest question marks has turned into one of the team’s most confident players. Despite having doubts around Terence Steele at right tackle, Tyler Guyton has done everything the right way this offseason to be the left tackle of the Dallas Cowboys. Brian Schottenheimer recently discussed his resurgence . “Probably that second week of training camp is where we were like ‘whoa.’ It was just the way the confidence that he was taking in his sets and the counters that he was countering so when a defensive end rushes up field and tries to counter and go inside, he has the ability to move his feet inside and slam the door shut on that. Going up against different guys and watching him go up against different guys like Eze, watching him go up against RG and Malachi, and guys like that. You saw a guy that was beginning to understand the matchup element…” QUINNEN WILLIAMS: COWBOYS DEFENSE IS ‘NIGHT AND DAY’ DIFFERENT UNDER NEW DC CHRISTIAN PARKER – Kevin Patra, NFL.com We all assume the Cowboys defense will improve in 2026. But it’s always nice to hear the best defender on the roster see’s a night and day difference between the 2025 Cowboys defense and the 2026 Cowboys defense. Quinnen Williams joined the Dallas Cowboys for seven forgettable games in 2025 following his trade deadline deal . Even with the four-time Pro Bowler, the Cowboys defense stunk up the joint last season. In the months since, the 28-year-old has seen a distinct turnaround under new defensive coordinator Christian Parker. “The growth, it’s like night and day,” Williams said of the strides made by the Cowboys on defense, via the team’s official website . “Starting in OTAs, and starting the first week of training camp, getting a chance to go against one of the best offenses in battle every single day has helped us tremendously. The mindset coming from the coaches, top down to the players and to the leadership, has been drastically changed. It’s just fun, man. “I just can’t wait to see the process and the results from all the hard work, but we’re not done yet.” Predicting the 5 Dallas Cowboys players that won’t suit up for gameday in Week 1 vs. New York Giants – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Dallas It’s never too early to take a look at the possible gameday inactives for week one. Mauricio Rodriguez takes a stab at what the inactive list may look like on Sunday Night Football in a little over a week. DT Jonathan Bullard: The Cowboys are betting on Bullard’s experience and versatility. But he hasn’t practiced since Aug. 4 due to injury (groin/core) and I believe there will be a ramp up period before he plays. With Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark spearheading the group, I think the Cowboys can be patient with him. OL Drew Shelton: The fourth-round rookie is not NFL ready. His struggles in the preseason cannot be ignored by the Cowboys and I wouldn’t expect him to play early on. Can he develop into a starting tackle? Maybe. But it will take time. For now, Shelton might be looking at many “healthy scratch” games barring any injuries. Daily discussion question: What is your most conservative prediction for this season?

title: Sean Payton comments on Broncos’ focus competing in a ‘real good’ division
summary: The regular season is literally just days away and the Denver Broncos are trying to follow up a 14-3 season with one that matches or beats it. The challenge is significant. Of the 36 teams who have won 14 or more games in a regular season, only two (’89 49ers and ‘03 Patriots) have won […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Head Coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos walks on the sidelines during the second quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The regular season is literally just days away and the Denver Broncos are trying to follow up a 14-3 season with one that matches or beats it. The challenge is significant. Of the 36 teams who have won 14 or more games in a regular season, only two (’89 49ers and ‘03 Patriots) have won at least that many games the following season . To make things even more difficult, the Broncos are playing in an AFC West that is considered to be stacked with talent this season. Head coach Sean Payton said that now that they’ve won the AFC west they must find a way to stay there. “There’s a history with all those division opponents and usually you have to find a way to beat the one that’s at the top,” Payton said this week. “So that was our task right away, it was Kansas City. They had won this division however many years in a row… We’re competing in a real good division. You just look around, everyone has gotten better. The focus more is internal, our improvement and playing well.” So while it would be great to see Denver win another 14 games this season, it isn’t necessary to take care of business in their division. Win the division first. Then worry about playoff seeding. A lot must go right for a 14+ win season, but you don’t need a 14+ win season to in titles. Horse Tracks

title: Broncos vs Chiefs is loaded with storylines, but Denver is keeping its focus internal
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! The storylines for the Denver Broncos opener are thoroughly rich. It’s the first game of the season, against a hated division rival, on the road, on Monday Night Football, with their star quarterback returning from injury, against an opponent looking to rebound from a tough season, while Denver looks to start […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 25: Zach Allen #99 of the Denver Broncos lines up before the snap during the AFC Championship NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! The storylines for the Denver Broncos opener are thoroughly rich. It’s the first game of the season, against a hated division rival, on the road, on Monday Night Football, with their star quarterback returning from injury, against an opponent looking to rebound from a tough season, while Denver looks to start strong after a very good previous season. In other words, bring on Sept. 14 in Kansas City. “I think it’s going to be really cool, definitely get the season going,” Broncos defensive lineman Zach Allen said to the media earlier this week. “It’s good we have at least a little extra time to prepare for such a good opponent, and to do it on primetime is really cool. Division games are awesome, and the history between the two organizations amps it up even more. I’m really excited.” The fact that the Broncos open against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs just makes the next week and a half even more important. To really dial in and get as prepared as Denver can. “It’s huge. I think every week is about getting better,” Broncos right tackle Mike McGlinchey said to the media. “We’ve done that since we started training camp. This week is no exception. You don’t want to go into a game week next week off of a three-day off day and not feel like you accomplished something the week before or get better at your job. “I think it’s an incredible opportunity we have for the next three days to go and compete against each other for a couple more times here, hone in on some of the small details, kind of the introductions to what we want to do in the game plan against Kansas City, and then hit the ground running. Like I said, you want to be your best on Week 1, but it’s more important to be your best in Week 18. Every single week, you have to be better than the week before. It’s not going to be perfect when we first go out and start, but it’s about continuing to improve on each rep and each game as the season unfolds.” For Broncos head coach Sean Payton, the message is simple. It’s not about the Chiefs, the rivalry, or the opener; it’s about what the Broncos do. “There’s a history with all those division opponents, and usually you have to find a way to beat the one that’s at the top. So that was our task right away: it was Kansas City. They had won this division however many years in a row. So then, when you win it, now you’ve got to find a way to stay there. It’s pretty much the case around the league. “In New Orleans, I don’t know how many different division coaches that we saw. Tampa was the team that had won the Super Bowl, I think, in 2002. Early on, that was the team that you had to find a way to get past them. So that’s kind of where I see us right now. We’re competing in a real good division. You just look around, everyone has gotten better. The focus more is internal, our improvement and playing well. That’s kind of how I see it.”

full_text: It’s Week 1 of the college football season, which means it is time to start tracking which 2027 NFL Draft prospects could be the best fits for the Detroit Lions. Unlike most NFL Draft-centric college football previews, the primary focus here is not to tell you which players are the top, most athletically gifted prospects. Of course, talent, athleticism, and draft-worthiness are part of the analysis; the focus is on which prospects best fit the Detroit Lions and the culture of high-intangible, strong football character built during the Dan Campbell and Brad Holmes era. This is the Grit Index. The Grit Index In 2023, Erik Schlitt and I developed the Grit Index as a metric to quantify what grit means for the Detroit Lions through intangible traits. Since then, we’ve seen increasing success in predicting which players the Lions will covet as we continue to fine-tune our criteria. This is one reason we were able to identify Blake Miller as a fit early in the offseason this past draft cycle. The inaugural Grit Index was simply a list of players with strong intangible profiles in Dane Brugler’s annual The Beast . That inaugural list included Lions draft picks Jack Campbell, Sam LaPorta, and Brian Branch. In 2024, the Grit Index evolved into a tiered system , identifying Lions selections Sione Vaki and Mekhi Wingo as Tier 1 prospects, along with Terrion Arnold and UDFAs Isaiah Williams and Kingsley Eguakun in Tier 3. Then in 2025, the Grit Index took another step forward by assigning prospects a numerical score from 0-100 . That version identified several future Lions, including Tate Ratledge (86.3) , Ahmed Hassanein (79.35), Isaac TeSlaa (77.36), and Dan Jackson (76.33). The most recent evolution came in 2026 , when we refined the scoring system to a 0-10 scale and incorporated positional considerations to better compare players across the board. That refinement identified Blake Miller with a 9.67 score, placing him in the “upper elite” tier. Keith Abney (9.07) and Skyler Gill-Howard (9.42) also ranked highly. title: The Detroit Lions may be over the salary cap by next week
summary: When the NFL shifts from the offseason to the regular season, the accounting for the salary cap changes—and it can have a dramatic impact on where a team’s standing is when it comes to cap compliance. During the offseason—when teams have a 90-man roster—only the top 51 contracts count against the salary cap. But when […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - MAR 01: Brad Holmes, general manager of the Detroit Lions speaks to reporters during the NFL Draft Combine at the Indiana Convention Center on March 1, 2022 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the NFL shifts from the offseason to the regular season, the accounting for the salary cap changes—and it can have a dramatic impact on where a team’s standing is when it comes to cap compliance. During the offseason—when teams have a 90-man roster—only the top 51 contracts count against the salary cap. But when teams cut down to 53-man rosters, suddenly every contract counts against the salary cap. That includes not only the 53 players on the active roster, but also the 16 players on the practice squad, players on injured reserve or PUP/NFI, and all the dead money from terminated contracts. When it comes to the Detroit Lions, during the “top-51” offseason calculation, they had just over $10 million in cap space, according to the latest NFLPA public salary cap report . But on Monday—the official start of Week 1—the NFL will switch over to every contract counting, and according to the cap experts at Over The Cap, that switch could put the Lions over the salary cap. Jason Fitzgerald, who runs Over the Cap, switched over the accounting on his site to reflect the regular season salary cap rules, and although he admits some of the most recent transactions aren’t yet considered (he says he’s “about a day behind on waivers”), he projects the Lions to be about $3 million over the cap. You can see Fitzgerald’s complete breakdown of the Lions’ 2026 salary cap here . How can the Lions be over the cap? Well, they can’t be. By Monday, they will have to become cap-compliant. That could mean cutting a few players and creating some extra space— they may have already started this by releasing Seth McLaughlin and Jabari Small . But, more likely, it will mean restructuring some contracts not only to get cap-compliant, but also to free up some needed cap space during the season. For example, when a player goes on injured reserve during the season, they get paid in full, but Detroit would need to find money to pay their replacement on the 53-man roster. Obviously, the Lions would also want flexibility at the trade deadline or for any other players who may become available during the season. But hold on… One thing to consider is that Fitzgerald’s calculations also include $6.66 million in dead cap from Terrion Arnold’s contract. As we pointed out in June, that number reflects the dead cap hit on Arnold’s contract if the Lions did not try to void his guarantees . At this point, we don’t have public information on whether Detroit is attempting to recoup those guarantees, but based on their history of conduct, there’s a pretty good chance they are. There’s also an equally likely chance that Arnold will try to file a grievance over that. If he does that, the Lions will be charged 40% of the contested salary against the salary cap until a ruling is made. From there, the Lions are either credited with cap space or face additional cap commitments based on the arbitration ruling. Regardless of how Arnold’s situation is playing out behind the financial scenes, Detroit is still likely to create some cap space. Generally speaking, they like to carry between $10-20 million in cap space during the season, and even if Arnold’s salary is off the books, that’s likely not enough space for Brad Holmes and company to be comfortable. How can the Lions become cap compliant? Easy: restructures. This offseason, they already did a partial restructure of Jared Goff’s contract . But there is still about $14 million of his salary that can be turned into a signing bonus, which would free up almost $12 million on its own. Penei Sewell’s $19.9 million salary is also ripe for restructuring, as is Amon-Ra St. Brown’s $27.5 million salary. In short, there are plenty of ways for Detroit to easily get under the cap. The question is which contract(s) they’ll use, and how much of that salary cap hit they choose to kick down the road. So, who cares? Fair point; the Lions will surely work this out. But I think this is just another reminder that Detroit is tighter against the cap than most people are considering. Yes, they have mechanisms to create as much cap space as they want this year, but that is going to continually come at the cost of future cap space.

title: What uniform combination should the Lions go with against the Saints?
summary: We are nearly there. After the coming weekend, we will officially be into Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. For the Detroit Lions, that means hosting the New Orleans Saints back in the friendly confines of Ford Field. It’s a big season for Detroit in many ways, and after a 2025 season that fell […]
full_text: We are nearly there. After the coming weekend, we will officially be into Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. For the Detroit Lions, that means hosting the New Orleans Saints back in the friendly confines of Ford Field. It’s a big season for Detroit in many ways, and after a 2025 season that fell short of everyone’s expectations—I expect the team to come out of the gates with a sizable chip on their shoulders. However, we still have over a week to get into all of the analysis and preparation for the game against New Orleans. So for now, let’s get into something that doesn’t matter very much at all, and yet many of us still care—uniforms. There was and still are plenty of discussions taking place surrounding the unveiling of the Lions’ 2026 Rivalry jerseys . Rather than jumping into those waters, let’s focus on another hotly debated topic amongst varying generations of fans: the silver pants. For a while now, the team has taken a liking to the monochromatic look where they have on all one color: the “blueberries” at home where they rock the blue home jersey with the blue pants, or the stormtrooper look on the road with the white on white. Listen, I like both of those looks, and they have their places, but please, wear the silver pants more often. At home, on the road. Both, if we are feeling crazy. And that brings us to today’s question of the day—what uniform combination do you want the Lions to wear in Week 1? My answer: You probably could have guessed this, but the blue tops with the silver pants. Lions coach Dan Campbell has put it out there before that the captains make the decisions for jerseys, and while I am also superstitious, let’s just try the traditional home look in Week 1. See how it goes and then we can go from there. Penei Sewell, Amon-Ra St. Brown, and the other captains, if you are reading this for whatever reason, do it for the 80s and 90s babies. What about you? What jerseys do you want the Lions to wear in Week 1 against the Saints? Let us know in the poll and comments below.

title: Referee announced for Packers’ Week 1 matchup vs. Vikings
summary: The NFL has announced its Week 1 referee assignments, and the Green Bay Packers, who will open the season against the Minnesota Vikings in Minneapolis, will start the year with Shawn Hochuli. Hochuli’s crews have been known to be flag-happy, as they are the only ones to have ranked among the top four in the […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - DECEMBER 21: Referee Shawn Hochuli #83 announces a penalty during the third quarter of a game between the Denver Broncos and the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High on December 21, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL has announced its Week 1 referee assignments, and the Green Bay Packers, who will open the season against the Minnesota Vikings in Minneapolis, will start the year with Shawn Hochuli. Hochuli’s crews have been known to be flag-happy, as they are the only ones to have ranked among the top four in the NFL in flags thrown per game in back-to-back seasons. Hochuli only worked one Packers game last year, their win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8. In that game, Hochuli’s team threw 11 flags — one of their lowest marks of the regular season — for 112 total yards (two penalties were declined). Overall, Hochuli’s crew worked 17 regular-season games last year and only threw fewer than double-digit flags just once, an eight-flag affair between the Denver Broncos and Jacksonville Jaguars. For what it’s worth, the Packers ranked 14th in the NFL in penalties in 2025, and the Vikings weren’t far behind them in 16th place. Last year, Hochuli’s crew didn’t call roughing the passer, unnecessary roughness, offensive pass interference or defensive pass interference at the rate of other crews, but they did throw flags on neutral zone infractions, illegal blocks above the waist, intentional groundings and defensive holdings well above the league’s per-game averages. If you’re going to guess how many flags Hochuli throws next Sunday, double digits is probably the baseline you’re going to want to start from.

title: Josh Jacobs’ initial hearing has been moved up by several months
summary: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was placed on the NFL’s commissioner exempt list before the league’s final cutdowns to teams’ initial 53-man rosters for the 2026 season. The Packers’ brass has stated that they will stand by Jacobs, who is currently set to face charges of battery and criminal damage in Brown County, […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JUNE 09: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers participates in drills during the Green Bay Packers mandatory minicamp at Don Hutson Center on June 09, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was placed on the NFL’s commissioner exempt list before the league’s final cutdowns to teams’ initial 53-man rosters for the 2026 season. The Packers’ brass has stated that they will stand by Jacobs, who is currently set to face charges of battery and criminal damage in Brown County , while the legal process plays out. On Friday, we learned that the legal process might end up taking less time than we originally thought. When Brown County officially announced what Jacobs was going to be charged with by the district attorney’s office last month, Jacobs’ initial hearing for his case was set for November 17th. According to Fox 11 News , court records now show that Jacobs’ initial hearing has been pushed up to September 10th, just days before the Packers’ season-opening game against the Minnesota Vikings — though Fox 11 News reported that Jacobs is unlikely to make an appearance in court for the start of the legal process. The outlet received an authorization to appear and act document, which Jacobs filed with the state of Wisconsin on Wednesday, stating that his attorneys can act on his behalf while he opts to not attend the hearing — an option he has since his charges are misdemeanors. Don’t expect a bow to be tied on this case after just the initial hearing, but the legal process does seem to be happening quicker than we originally expected.

title: Packers Preview: What to expect from a MarShawn Lloyd running game?
summary: The Green Bay Packers’ running game is going to be a bit of a mystery box going into the 2026 regular season. Not only is starting running back Josh Jacobs on the commissioner exempt list, but the players who will backfill Jacobs’ carries have never been significant ball-carriers at the NFL level, and the Packers’ […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 21: Green Bay Packers running back Marshawn Lloyd (32) carries the ball in the first quarter during a preseason game between the Green Bay Packers and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Green Bay Packers’ running game is going to be a bit of a mystery box going into the 2026 regular season. Not only is starting running back Josh Jacobs on the commissioner exempt list , but the players who will backfill Jacobs’ carries have never been significant ball-carriers at the NFL level, and the Packers’ offensive line is in a bit of a transition. If you missed the news this summer, let’s catch you up on what’s going on with Green Bay’s run game. Josh Jacobs First of all, the reason that MarShawn Lloyd is likely to be the Packers’ top ball-carrier to start the year is that Jacobs has been charged with battery and criminal damage to property in an incident that involved his girlfriend. This alleged incident occurred in May, but Jacobs wasn’t officially charged by Brown County until August 27th, as the district attorney’s office waited to make a judgment until they received a surveillance video and passed it through a digital forensic examination report, which “was complex and took several weeks.” As of now, Jacobs is on the commissioner exempt list, which means that he is allowed to attend meetings in the facility — which the team has confirmed he is doing — but is not allowed to practice or play for the Packers until he’s taken off the list. Currently, there is no timetable for when Jacobs’ situation will be resolved. An initial hearing , not a sentencing, is scheduled for Jacobs’ case on November 17th. The Packers have said they will let the legal process play out. Josh Jacobs’ replacements At the moment, the Packers are carrying three running backs on the 53-man roster, since Jacobs is on the exempt list: MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks. Lloyd has played 10 regular-season snaps (all from one game) going into Year 3 of his pro career, as he’s dealt with a series of unfortunate injuries after being picked in the third round by the Packers back in 2024. At the moment, he’s expected to be Green Bay’s top ball-carrier going into the 2026 season, at least until Jacobs returns (if he does return). Backing him up are Johnson, a 2025 third-round pick who was traded from the Pittsburgh Steelers to the Packers at the cutdown deadline for a 2028 sixth-round pick, and Brooks. Johnson averaged 2.8 carries per game as a rookie for the Steelers last year. For what it’s worth, Johnson also played under offensive coordinator Tim Lester, a former analyst under head coach Matt LaFleur, at the University of Iowa. Brooks is more of a blocking back than a ball-carrier, as he’s carried the ball on just 16 percent of the offensive plays that he’s been on the field for (63 of 387) over the last two regular seasons. Books has averaged about two carries per game in Green Bay. The scheme transition MarShawn Lloyd's preseason carries pic.twitter.com/GjErUGGTkE — Justis Mosqueda (@JuMosq) September 4, 2026 The biggest difference between the Packers’ offense in the preseason and what we’ve seen in recent years is that the team leaned into the outside/mid zone scheme much more heavily this summer. It appears that the offense is transitioning back into what it looked like in the earlier LaFleur years, where they were asking their linemen to make more athletic plays in space, rather than just trying to get vertical displacement on inside runs. You can see how frequently Green Bay ran stretch plays, a LaFleur staple when he had Aaron Jones in the backfield instead of Jacobs, with Lloyd in the clip linked above. We’ve mentioned that this is a possibility, as it stuck out like a sore thumb in the preseason. Over the last week, both LaFleur and general manager Brian Gutekunst have mentioned the team leaning into “outside zone stuff” in press conferences. This should also improve the play-action game, as the Packers pair their naked bootlegs with outside zone runs, something that hasn’t really been a big part of Green Bay’s offense since Jacobs arrived. The offensive line At the moment, the expectation right now is that the team’s starting offensive line will be Jordan Morgan, Aaron Banks, Sean Rhyan, Jacob Monk and Zach Bako-Bewele (formerly Tom) from left to right. With that being said, both Banks (tendinitis) and Bako-Bewele (post-surgery from a partially torn patellar tendon) are dealing with knee injuries that have limited their participation throughout training camp. According to LaFleur, it’s not clear whether or not Bank or Bako-Bewele can play 60-minute football games right now , so their status going into Week 1 of the regular season is very much up in the air. If they can’t go against the Minnesota Vikings, the expected Banks replacement would be fifth-round rookie Jager Burton, and the expected Bako-Bewele replacement would be second-year second-round pick Anthony Belton. — With all of this laid out, how do you think the Packers’ running game will fare this regular season? title: Packers can be optimistic about forcing turnovers in 2026
summary: A little over a year ago, I wrote about the Packers’ defense and its plans for 2025. Heading into the second year of the Jeff Hafley era, the Packers wanted to force even more turnovers than they had in 2024, which I argued was an admirable but misguided plan. “Get more turnovers” isn’t really a […]
full_text: Sep 21, 2025; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; Green Bay Packers safety Xavier McKinney (29) intercepts a pass by the Cleveland Browns during the second quarter at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Scott Galvin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A little over a year ago, I wrote about the Packers’ defense and its plans for 2025 . Heading into the second year of the Jeff Hafley era, the Packers wanted to force even more turnovers than they had in 2024, which I argued was an admirable but misguided plan. “Get more turnovers” isn’t really a strategy, because it’s not really something teams can control, at least not in the same way they can control other aspects of defensive performance. A year later, planning to bolster the Packers’ defensive performance by increasing their turnovers is still a bad plan — but it may have a better chance of working this year, though not because of anything the Packers will do. My colleague Paul Noonan recently wrote a terrific piece about the Chicago Bears. You should go read it , then send it to your friends who root for the Bears and get them to read it, too. They’ll love it, and they’ll definitely appreciate Paul’s thoughtful critique and adjust their expectations for 2026 accordingly. They’ll probably thank you for it, honestly. Anyhow, buried in that piece is this nugget: Turnovers are not ALL about luck, but the Bears were extremely lucky on fumble recoveries, and while interceptions involve more skill than fumble recoveries do, they managed an incredible 32.4% interception rate on their passes defended, easily leading the league. No other team was above 25%, and the league average is closer to 20%. That data comes from the FTN Football Almanac and, in addition to telling us about the Bears, can also tell us a bit about the Packers. The calculation for interception rate is pretty simple: you divide a team’s total interceptions by their total number of passes defensed. The almanac draws its data from charting by Sports Information Solutions, so its passes defensed numbers are a bit lower than official NFL stats or ones you might see somewhere like Pro Football Reference, but the general idea holds: when they got their hands on the ball on defense, the 2025 Chicago Bears converted a disproportionate number of those opportunities into turnovers. The Packers, however, did not. In 2025, according to numbers from Pro Football Reference, the Packers recorded seven interceptions against 59 passes defensed, a rate of just 11.86%. The league average, according again to Pro Football Reference, was 16.1%. The Packers, according to the numbers, were a bit unlucky in the interception department. That tracks with their overall regression on turnovers last season. In 2024, bolstered by Xavier McKinney intercepting everything in sight, the Packers were well above the league average for turnovers forced. But in 2025, they cratered — only four players caught an interception in 2025 at all, and only McKinney and Evan Williams nabbed more than one. This shouldn’t have been a surprise to anyone paying attention. It’s very unusual for a team to outproduce the league average in turnovers in consecutive years. The Packers have only done it once in the Matt LaFleur era (2021 and 2022), the first times they’ve done it since the Charles Woodson/Nick Collins maximum ballhawking era. Fortunately, there’s reason to be optimistic for 2026. Though nobody’s ever “due” for interceptions (the pesky Gambler’s Fallacy has something to say about that), the Packers have never really been consistently below average forcing interceptions, either. Here are their year-by-year interception ratio numbers for the Matt LaFleur era. If FTN’s 20% interception to passes defensed ratio is accurate (give or take, factoring in differences between statistical sources), I think we can expect the Packers to have a good shot at outperforming their 2025 interception ratio. The odds seem pretty good that the Packers’ interception totals will tick up in 2026. They still shouldn’t bank on turnovers alone for better defensive outcomes this season, but there’s good reason to think more picks will come their way. Even if the Packers are merely average in that department, they’ll produce more turnovers this season than last.
