title: The Packers’ 2026 schedule is mostly friendly for out-of-market fans across the US
summary: Being a fan of one of the NFL’s biggest fan bases has its perks. For Green Bay Packers fans living in the United States but outside of the team’s home television markets, nationally televised games are a welcome sight. Fans can certainly debate the time slot that they prefer based on their own circumstances, but […]
full_text: Nov 15, 2015; Green Bay, WI, USA; A FOX TV camera hangs over the field during warmups prior to the game between the Detroit Lions and Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Detroit won 18-16. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Being a fan of one of the NFL’s biggest fan bases has its perks. For Green Bay Packers fans living in the United States but outside of the team’s home television markets, nationally televised games are a welcome sight. Fans can certainly debate the time slot that they prefer based on their own circumstances, but one thing is certain: if you don’t live in Wisconsin, more prime time games means it’s easier and cheaper to see every Packers game on TV than if you were, say, a Las Vegas Raiders fan living outside of the American Southwest. This season, the Packers should have roughly two-thirds of their regular season schedule available to all — or nearly all — American football fans via local TV or national streaming services. It’s those other games where local channels are likely to have other games that become the biggest challenge, and for Packers fans outside of the team’s home media market, it’s worth giving a bit of forethought to how to tune in. Prime time games aren’t in consideration here. One way or another, those games are readily available to any American football fan, regardless of location. This season, more so than others, will require some streaming subscriptions to get them all, but you can focus on just two: Prime Video and Netflix. Instead, let’s focus on the NFL’s typical Sunday afternoon schedule, starting with a refresher on how the league’s conventional television broadcast deal works. Each of FOX and CBS get a minimum of one game in every television market, with one of the two networks carrying a second game. Generally, the doubleheader alternates between the two networks, though in Weeks 1 and 18 they both have rights to broadcast games in both time slots. Generally, the network with the doubleheader will try to put its “Game of the Week” in that afternoon slot. Because fewer games kick off later — generally, only these big matchups or games taking place in the Pacific or Mountain time zones get the late afternoon slot — the bigger matchup goes out to as many stations across the country as possible to maximize viewership. There are simply more games played in the early Sunday time slot than the late afternoon, and therefore there more opportunities for a local station to carry a different game. Of course, the NFL does have one authorized option for watching Sunday games that are not available on your local TV affiliates: NFL Sunday Ticket. However, that can be an extremely expensive option, as it costs $240 for the whole season for new subscribers or $378 for returning users. Unlike last season, the service does not offer a monthly subscription option that can be canceled That’s a hefty price for plenty of football fans, which could drive them to local restaurants or bars instead of the comfort of home. However, as mentioned earlier, out-of-market Packers fans will have a minimal need for Sunday Ticket in 2026. Barring games being flexed out of their current time slots, the Packers have a whopping six prime time games this season, four more 3:25 PM kickoffs, and one noon game that is on a holiday and is there guaranteed to be available nationwide. That leaves only five games currently scheduled for the early Sunday time slot, with the kickoff time in week 18 as always to be determined. Of course, the NFL’s aggressive expansion into streaming services make it somewhat more expensive to watch all of these “nationally broadcast” games. That is especially so for the Packers, who will have a whopping four of their 17 regular season games available exclusively on streaming platforms. Green Bay plays twice on Thursday Night Football, which is shown on Prime Video, while the games on Wednesday of Thanksgiving week and Christmas Day will be on Netflix. Yes, that means fans outside of Green Bay and Milwaukee will need two streaming subscriptions over the course of the season. But if timed right, those subscription fees are much less expensive than a full year of NFL Sunday Ticket. Let’s look at the schedule week-by-week to see the few instances when a Sunday Ticket subscription is likely to come in handy. Let’s look at each of the Sunday afternoon games — both early and late — to see what other games they will be up against and whether the Packers’ contest is likely to be a top matchup. Week 1: @ Vikings, 3:25 PM — Game of the Week The opening week is one of the few that feature both networks getting a doubleheader. CBS picked Packers-Vikings as its highlight game in the late afternoon, with only one other contest (Cardinals vs. Chargers) up against it on CBS. FOX does have two as well: Commanders vs. Eagles and Dolphins vs. Raiders. Blackout rules might mean that the home markets for those teams could have CBS blacked out, but this should be a very widely shown game as long as you’re not in the southwest. Week 2: @ Jets, 12:00 PM — Regional Broadcast FOX has the doubleheader in week 2, so most markets will get one of the four total games in this time slot, with Vikings-Bears likely to be the biggest matchup. That will likely have the widest distribution, so expect to make alternate arrangements if you’re outside of the Wisconsin or New York City markets. Week 4: @ Buccaneers, 12:00 PM — Regional Broadcast The entire NFL early slate is stacked this week. Along with this game, FOX has Cowboys-Texans, Rams-Eagles, and Jets-Bears, with the first two of those being great matchups that should dominate the landscape. CBS has the doubleheader, however, meaning the Dolphins-Vikings contest at 3:05 PM will also be competing for eyeballs. This game is probably the one least likely to show up on your local station if you live outside of Wisconsin (or, in this case, Florida). Week 5: vs. Bears, 3:25 PM — Game of the Week Surprisingly, FOX has to air two other games alongside Packers-Bears, which is one of that network’s biggest games of the year on the heels of last year’s Wild Card game. 49ers-Seahawks and Lions-Cardinals are also on the network in that time slot, but expect the NFC North showdown to be aired across most of the rest of the country. Week 7: @ Lions, 3:25 PM — Game of the Week This one will be almost everywhere. The only markets that should see a different game on FOX at that time will be LA and Las Vegas, which should get the Rams-Raiders game. Week 9: @ Patriots, 3:25 PM — Game of the Week As was the case two weeks earlier, this contest will only have one other game to compete with on FOX, this one being Cardinals-Seahawks. Week 10: vs. Vikings, 12:00 PM — Regional Broadcast For only the third time in the first ten weeks, the Packers play at noon. On paper, this seems like the best game on FOX in the early slot, however; Panthers-Saints, Texans-Browns, and Jaguars-Titans don’t feature many fan bases on the level of the Packers, and the NFC North is still expected to be one of the best divisions in football. FOX also has the doubleheader, so no competing with any games in the late time slot. Expect a good portion of the country to get this game locally. Week 13: @ Saints, 12:00 PM — Regional Broadcast This week is a bit tougher to predict than many of the others. It’s on FOX, but CBS has the doubleheader. That makes it one of five games over two time slots that channels have to pick from, a group that includes the following: 49ers-Giants (Noon), Jaguars-Bears (Noon), Eagles-Cardinals (3:05), and Dolphins-Broncos (3:05). It’s anyone’s guess if any of these will end up being a big draw, so don’t count on getting Green Bay’s game this week. Week 15: vs. Dolphins, 12:00 PM — Regional Broadcast As in Week 15, this game also competes with four others for viewership on FOX in a non-doubleheader week, but none of them jump out on paper — in part because the NFL put a…

title: The Madden Curse is real and it’s coming for the Bears
summary: I live in suburban Chicago Illinois, which has several benefits. One of the big benefits is that I get to hear overconfident Bears fans on the radio, which I enjoy more than hearing overconfident Green Bay Packers fans on the radio. Don’t get me wrong, I’m not at all against proclaiming the superiority of your […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 18: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears looks on during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Rams in the NFC Divisional Playoffs at Soldier Field on January 18, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images I live in suburban Chicago Illinois, which has several benefits. One of the big benefits is that I get to hear overconfident Bears fans on the radio, which I enjoy more than hearing overconfident Green Bay Packers fans on the radio. Don’t get me wrong, I’m not at all against proclaiming the superiority of your football team when it’s warranted, but when I listen to Wisconsin sports radio the, ahem, “quality” of callers praising the team often has me questioning whether the Packers are actually any good at all. Here in Chicagoland, it works in reverse. The vast, vast majority of the city is convinced of three things: Caleb is DEFINITELY the man. It. The promised one. And at the very least, he is superior to Jordan Love. The Bears are legitimate Super Bowl contenders, and possibly at the beginning of a dynasty. No other team in the division is even close. These all seem…how to put this delicately…“not true.” Or, less delicately, “delusional.” The Bears had a very good, very fun season in 2025, but I spend most of my time writing about luck and regression to the mean and the like, and let me tell you, if the Packers were coming off of the season that the Bears just had, I would be in full fledged panic mode. I already have a bit of a reputation as a Debbie Downer and if the Packers and Bears switched places I’d reach new levels of doomsaying. I would be researching top five picks in the 2027 draft already. I mean, if we had a first-round pick in that draft, I would be doing that, in this alternate universe which we are thankfully not in. It’s important to perform this mental exercise to ensure that 1 . I’m not just hating on the Bears because I do actually hate them and they’re a terrible franchise that’s probably moving to Indiana, or 2 . because the Brewers are facing the Cubs right now and I’m taking out my frustration at Cubs fans continually chanting “ Green Bay Sucks ” in between cheering for shallow flyouts they really thought were going to be home runs. Fortunately, you don’t have to take my word for it. We have neutral arbiters we can turn to for these questions, namely casinos! The team with the best betting odds to win the division isn’t the Bears, it’s the Lions, who sit at +145 at Fanduel. The Bears are also not second, falling short of the Packers (+160). They’re a comfortable third (+350), just ahead of the Vikings (+460). The venerable football analytics website FTN.com also projects the Bears for 9 wins and third place in the division behind the Lions (10.5 wins) and Packers (9.5), and just one game ahead of the Vikings (8). People wagering actual money or doing advanced math all kind of hate the Bears, and rightfully so. I’ve read plenty of offseason pieces poking holes in the Packers’ roster, but only a few on the Bears, so allow me to poke away. Regression to the Mean Comes for Us All First, the Bears were super lucky last year. By Tom Bliss’ luck metrics, the Bears were the eighth-luckiest team in football (Minnesota was seventh), gaining basically half a win of Win Percentage Added (WPA) over the course of the season due to events completely outside of their control. Luck dashboard through week 17 Most impactful plays: – CHI dropped pass with 0:36 left in Q4 (+20.0% for SF) – LAR dropped pass with 10:09 left in Q4 (+18.8% for ATL) – ATL makes 51-yd FG with 0:25 left in Q4 (-17.6% for LAR) pic.twitter.com/9FqV0Pya9n — Tom Bliss (@DataWithBliss) December 30, 2025 You can also see this in their expected record versus their actual record (9.1-7.9 versus their actual 11-6), and the fact that they were third in the division in point differential, behind the Lions and Packers. Point differential predicts future win totals better than previous win totals predict future win totals (say that five times fast), and so bettors and nerds see the Bears as more of a true nine-win team). The Bears were also alarmingly lucky on defense. They were 30 th in yards per play allowed, they allowed the most explosive passing plays in the league, and they allowed a league-leading 13 passing touchdowns of 20+ yards. They allowed the most rushing yards before contact in the league and the fifth highest explosive run rate. They were terrible at everything that matters. The only reason they were not getting blown out week-in and week-out is turnovers. Turnovers are not ALL about luck, but the Bears were extremely lucky on fumble recoveries, and while interceptions involve more skill than fumble recoveries do, they managed an incredible 32.4% interception rate on their passes defended, easily leading the league. No other team was a bove 25%, and the league average is closer to 20%. Finally, the Bears were 26 th in the league in DVOA on first and second down, and shot up to ninth best on third and fourth down. FTN , who produced most of these statistics (buy their annual almanac here! ) has tracked this for at least two decades now, and when third down efficiency is vastly better than first and second down efficiency, the team’s defense almost always craters the following year, as those high leverage third down plays fall back to average (or worse). And while the Bears were staging all of those thrilling, but unsustainably lucky comeback wins, the Packers and Lions were getting phenomenally unlucky , ranking 29 th and 30 th in the Bliss rankings. The Lions were the only team to lose WPA in all four major luck categories, while the Packers experienced a lot of positive fumble luck, while giving it all back (and then some) on opposing field goals and opposing dropped passes. It’s one thing to be lucky while your major opponents are basically average. Instead, the Bears benefitted from their own luck, as well as colossal bad luck from their closest rivals. Caleb Williams Was “Fine” On offense, I think the Bears have outstanding personnel, especially at the skill positions, but anyone claiming the Caleb Williams is currently better than Jordan Love needs to put down the Malort and take a few deep breaths. Williams did a nice job making big plays, and those comebacks were all thrilling, but over the entire 60 minutes of a game, the man just wasn’t very good. Including the playoffs, Caleb Williams had a worse completion percentage last season than JJ McCarthy, and every other quarterback except Shedeur Sanders. He was just 13 th in yards per game (slightly ahead of Jordan Love and the slow-as-molasses Packers) while Jared Goff was 2 nd . He was 19 th in TD% (Love was 10 th , Goff was 6 th ). Caleb does at least have Love on some of the counting stats, as Love missed two games, and the Packers just don’t pass that much, but in the more advance stats, Love was third in Completion Percentage Over Expected (CPOE) to Caleb’s 29 th (Goff was 12 th ), and Love was fifth in Adjusted Net Yards per Attempt (ANY/A) to Williams’ 11 th (Goff was third). Love and Goff have better success rates, passer ratings, and Love even has Williams on Average Depth of Target. The only place where Williams clearly outperformed the league was in protecting the ball. Williams’ 1.2% INT% was truly special and led the league among qualified quarterbacks, but Love and Goff weren’t exactly butchers, ranking fifth and sixth respectively. Williams also led the league in fourth quarter comebacks, but it’s worth noting that he was one of the reasons they were so frequently behind in the first place. Now, this is all overly negative on Williams, and I actually like Williams as a prospect and expect he will improve into a truly dangerous quarterback. The fact of the matter is that he can make a lot of throws that other quarterbacks cannot, that I trust he will continue to make big plays a standard part of his game. He really only…

title: Weekend Musings: Some Houston Texans thoughts before the regular season
summary: Only 2 QBs total on the entire roster? The roster churn in the post-cutdown chaos is effectively over. Houston has its 53-man roster and 16-man practice squad situated. Yet, among all of the players that can call Houston their team, the squad will only have 2 active QBs (Stroud, Mills), and as of this writing, […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - AUGUST 28: Head coach DeMeco Ryans of the Houston Texans looks on during the first half of a preseason game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Only 2 QBs total on the entire roster? The roster churn in the post-cutdown chaos is effectively over. Houston has its 53-man roster and 16-man practice squad situated. Yet, among all of the players that can call Houston their team, the squad will only have 2 active QBs (Stroud, Mills), and as of this writing, ZERO QBs on the practice squad. The primary reason for that situation is that presumed QB3 Graham Mertz suffered a season-ending ACL tear in the 1st preseason game. QB Brett Rypien was called off the couch to play in Houston’s final two preseason games, but not 48 hours after his final play (strip-sack fumble), Rypien was gone. Granted, a QB3 is not usually the highest depth priority for a team. With Houston, depth pieces along the lines, defense and special teams ability dictated much of their personnel actions. While the Texans likely have a list of QB names they can call should the need arise to get an arm on the roster during the season, said player will likely be at more of a disadvantage if they take live snaps. Being a backup is hard enough, but it is that much harder if you are just trying to learn the playbook and lingo, to say nothing of diagnosing a complicated NFL defense. With Mertz on IR for the season, Houston might have at least considered one QB to store on the practice squad to have some familiarity with the system. Especially when you factor that Stroud has missed games in 2 of his 3 seasons due to concussions, Mills might have to play some games. If Mills is the sole QB option after Stroud, that can be a lot of risk for a team, even with a defense like Houston’s. Watch the O-line…again. Hasn’t that been the cry of this team for years? Fix the Oline. This offseason, Caserio used free agency and the draft (once again) to fortify that position. Yet, the projected starting Oline for Sept 13 has three holdovers from last season, and the two big free agent signings as either second string (Wyatt Teller at LG) or on IR (Braden Smith at RT). 1st round pick Keylan Rutledge at least locked down a spot at LG, but the enduring image of that so far was him getting planted on a play that went to the other side of the field. Neal Brown, a bargain-bin pickup, at least locked down the C position. Granted, when we did see the starting Oline in limited action in the preseason, they moved the ball fairly effectively. Will that be the case against Buffalo? Unfortunately, we will have to wait to see if this will work. The NFL to NCAA pipeline? If nothing else, college football’s “official” kickoff this weekend, along with the NFL starting next week, should drive a lot of the crazy non-playing stories further back in the sports pages. Yet, of all the crazy, the idea of NFL players returning to college to play football might be the looniest plotline out there. Then again, loony might be reality when Clemson kicks off against LSU this Saturday, when players that were in NFL training camps but days ago might suit up to play for LSU. Yes, there is a lot more to the story, between the clumsiness and ineffectiveness of the NCAA, the increasing role of judge-shopping to obtain a favorable ruling for a player and the financial incentives of the NIL era vs. salaries of NFL practice squad/back-of-the-depth chart players. No player that was in Texans training camp is involved in this situation at this point. Hopefully, this will die out after this season when the new NCAA eligibility rules kick in but talk about something that wasn’t on the bingo card to start the year. View Link Positive Reviews for the Rivalry Uniforms: In the never-ending quest for NFL teams to make more money to have something new and fresh for the fans, the Texans issued their “Rivalry” uniforms. Likely some of you have bought them, which Texans players will sport for games against rivals, like the Week 11 game vs. the Colts. While social media is mixed on the uniforms, “neutral” sports media sites are high on the new uniforms. That it is an homage to Houston car culture is a nice touch. Would it be better with more Columbia Blue? Of course. Then again, there is a rather, uh, colorful history about that color…one that is likely not disappearing anytime soon. Stroud Contract: Looks like Stroud is gambling on himself this season. After a series of back-and-forth media announcements, it seems clear that no new contract will get signed between the Stroud and the Texans before the start of the regular season. Based on various reports, Houston looked to offer Stroud ~$50M/year, keeping him well within the top 12 of QB salaries. Stroud’s camp was supposedly looking between $60M-$70M. Sometimes, such a bet can pay off (see Flacco, Joe in 2012). Then again, when you gamble, there is always a chance to lose. A promotion for a (former) Texan: Last season, JJ Watt was a full-time color analyst for CBS. On the #2 team with long-time broadcaster Ian Eagle, he got the chance to offer a D-Lineman perspective. Generally, the reviews were positive, especially as he wasn’t meant to be the face of the sports broadcast team for CBS. However, this past month, the man in the #1 color analyst spot, Tony Romo, was arrested for OWI in Wisconsin. CBS effectively suspended him indefinitely, leaving an opening for the #1 spot. What CBS’ long-term plans are for that spot, we don’t entirely know. Romo was not exactly in great standing over the past couple of years. However, the tandem of Eagle-Watt is being broken up, with Watt now taking the #1 analyst spot. Perhaps it helps that Watt isn’t a total TV rookie, but will CBS rue breaking up a fairly effective team? Also, we don’t know if Watt will cover that many Texans’ games, since he will be likely at the marquee/late-afternoon games. While Houston is good, they don’t usually get the 3:25 Central time slots on Sunday. This might hurt in another way. Houston was 4-0 in games Watt called last season. Just a few thoughts in the last week before our emotional well-being get dictated by the on-field performance of the Texans. Until then…

title: Texans quietly land high-upside DE Chris Braswell
summary: Once again, Nick Caserio made another under the radar, savvy move to bolder the roster. Chris Braswell was a five-star recruit out of high school but had to wait his turn behind a star-star-studed Alabama roster. Braswell replaced Will Anderson Jr. at Alabama as the Jack linebacker in their 3-4 front and didn’t disappoint. His […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 21: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens is pressured by Chris Braswell #43 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium on October 21, 2024 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images Once again, Nick Caserio made another under the radar, savvy move to bolder the roster. Chris Braswell was a five-star recruit out of high school but had to wait his turn behind a star-star-studed Alabama roster. Braswell replaced Will Anderson Jr. at Alabama as the Jack linebacker in their 3-4 front and didn’t disappoint. His impressive eight sacks and 10 tackles for loss were second on the team behind Dallas Turner who went 17th overall to the Vikings in 2024. He was a redshirt junior when he entered the draft after only one year of true production at Alabama. The NFL Stock Exchange podcast had him rated as the fourth and sixth defensive end in the 2024 class. They noted “how raw of a player” he was and that he is built exceptionally well, but lacked a “pass rush plan” and could only rush with power. A ‘toolsy” prospect with an Alabama pedigree, NFL stars have been made of much worse material. Peering back into my own draft analysis from 2o24, I noted that his pass rush ability was “simple” rather than nuanced. It didn’t shine off the tape like his counterpart Turner did. I thought he set the edge well, was asked to contain, but wasn’t the money-maker on defense. He would go on to be selected by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the second round. The limitations mentioned came true. His lack of a plan and limited bag of tricks made him easy to predict in the pass rush. At 6’3”, 250 pounds, he’s a thick and powerful edge but never earned a start in two seasons with Tampa Bay. A lack of production immediately soured his relationship with the coaching staff. It’s not as though the Bucs were great at rushing the passer either, Yaya Diaby led the team with seven sacks. His ineffectiveness lead to the team selecting Ruben Bain in the first round of this year’s draft. This was a critical offseason for him. Unfortunately, Braswell missed games two and three of the preseason, plus he was generally outplayed by David Walker and Anthony Nelson. The Bucs would release him, which meant they had no intention to sign him to their own practice squad. Braswell is a story of ‘what could have been’. It’s a classic tale of untapped potential that plagues many a prospect that enters the league. For the Buccaneers to quit on their second round pick after two seasons let’s you know their opinion of him. Two and a half sacks in two years doesn’t cut it and is why he was let go entirely. Haven't seen if it's an injury/to what extent it is that's keeping Chris Braswell out of practice but that's the one guy who cannot afford to miss any preseason action. Hanging on by a thread — Ashlie (@EMT_Ashlie) August 20, 2026 Now in Houston, he reunites with Will Anderson Jr and Logan Hall who played in Tampa Bay previously. Braswell will train as the team’s sole defensive end on the practice squad. Given the team’s recent score of injuries at the position, there’s a chance he could be elevated onto the roster in short order. Braswell played as an outside linebacker both at Alabama and Tampa Bay. Houston’s 4-3 defense would require him to set the edge more and rush the passer. It’s a great opportunity for Braswell to train, add to his repertoire, and turn into the player he was projected to be. If there’s an ecosystem for a raw linebacker to hone their craft, it’s Houston. For Houston, it’s a savvy, high-upside move that could pay off for both player and team. The Texans need depth at defensive end, and while he hasn’t been productive in his backup role, he’s a more than capable break-glass option. It will be intriguing to watch Braswell change schemes entering his third season. For now, he’s behind Dominique Robinson, UDFA Sebastian Harsh, and Jadeveon Clowney on the depth chart.

title: From trade bait to the Colts backup quarterback
summary: Is it a rags to riches story? Maybe not. Maybe it’s a riches to rags to riches again type of story: a redemption story. There is redemption in what Anthony Richardson has done to claim the backup quarterback role for the Indianapolis Colts. It is a story of redemption that isn’t quite complete, but it […]
full_text: Is it a rags to riches story? Maybe not. Maybe it’s a riches to rags to riches again type of story: a redemption story. There is redemption in what Anthony Richardson has done to claim the backup quarterback role for the Indianapolis Colts. It is a story of redemption that isn’t quite complete, but it is a lot closer to vindication than most thought it would ever get. In such a short period of time, Richardson has ridden the roller coaster that is the NFL and finds himself back on the rise. Look. Being the backup quarterback was never the goal, but sometimes priorities change and adjustments need to be made on the fly. Everyone has a path in life to follow. The NFL is no different. Richardson was supposed to be the guy, the franchise quarterback, until he wasn’t. Some players come in and take the league by storm. Others have a warming up period where they need to sit behind a veteran and learn. Others are thrown into a fire and burn out in their first stint but go on to greatness. Sam Darnold, anyone? Richardson’s path has been incredibly bumpy and undesirable, to say the least. His accuracy, maturity, and injuries have left something to be desired. He could have quit and walked away. He certainly could have sandbagged the Colts. He requested a trade, but he didn’t throw a major stink about it. A trade request was the right move. The actions taken after were even better. He rose to the occasion and took the opportunity before him. Being the backup was never the ultimate dream. It is, however, the next step in the process, and the next step towards ultimate redemption. What becomes of Anthony Richardson now? No one knows, not even Richardson. He doesn’t know the next moment, but he better be ready if it comes. He is one injury away from stepping foot on the field and resuming his role as the starting quarterback of the Colts. That is a sentence no one thought they would read five months ago, but that’s what redemption is all about.

title: Chiefs sign international tight end, release 3 from IR
summary: Friday’s official NFL transactions saw the Kansas City Chiefs host 10 players for tryouts and sign tight end Thomas Odukoya to the practice squad. Odukoya was born in Amsterdam but played American football at two junior colleges before landing at Eastern Michigan for four seasons. He joined the Tennessee Titans in 2022 as an International […]
full_text: Jul 24, 2025; Nashville, TN, USA; Tennessee Titans tight end Thomas Odukoya (89) makes a catch during training camp at Ascension Saint Thomas Sports Park. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Friday’s official NFL transactions saw the Kansas City Chiefs host 10 players for tryouts and sign tight end Thomas Odukoya to the practice squad. Odukoya was born in Amsterdam but played American football at two junior colleges before landing at Eastern Michigan for four seasons. He joined the Tennessee Titans in 2022 as an International Pathway Player. He has appeared in two NFL games. Per Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest , Odukoya has signed to Kansas City’s practice squad with an international player exemption, allowing the Chiefs to keep a 17th player on the unit. The Chiefs have kept tackle Chu Godrick as an exempted international player for the past three seasons. However, after appearing in four games last season, Godrick was claimed off waivers by the Miami Dolphins earlier this week. On Friday, the Chiefs reached injury settlements with three players who were waived/injured during Sunday’s final roster cuts. Quarterback Chris Oladokun, guard CJ Hanson and running back EJ Smith have all been waived from Kansas City’s Reserve/Injured (IR) list. Players with less than four accrued seasons who are cut while injured revert to a team’s IR if unclaimed on waivers. An injury settlement has the player and team negotiate an estimated recovery timeframe and pay a prorated portion of base salary to cover the expected missed weeks. The covered timeline rarely becomes public. After the settlement expires, Oladokun, Hanson and Smith will be free to join the active roster or practice squad of any of the NFL’s other 31 teams. A return to Kansas City will not be possible for an additional three weeks after that.

title: Chiefs schedule: Game-by-game predictions for the 2026 season
summary: The premise of this article is pretty straightforward. We’re going to go game by game and predict whether the Kansas City Chiefs are going to win or lose each week. Here’s an attempt at an honest look at where the Chiefs are now that the preseason is behind us. So, in the words of the […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Quarterback Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs watches NFL preseason game action in the fourth quarter against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The premise of this article is pretty straightforward. We’re going to go game by game and predict whether the Kansas City Chiefs are going to win or lose each week. Here’s an attempt at an honest look at where the Chiefs are now that the preseason is behind us. So, in the words of the legendary referee of MTV’s “Celebrity Deathmatch,” Mills Lane , “let’s get it on!” Kansas City Chiefs — 2026 Regular-Season Schedule Week 1: vs. Denver Broncos Right off the bat, we get a game that could decide the fate of the division. There are a couple of things the Chiefs have going for them in this one. 1. It will be quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ first game back from injury, and I expect him to be highly motivated. 2. I have faith in the Chiefs’ improved secondary to limit what Dever can do through the air. Still, Denver boasts one of the best defenses in the NFL. My gut says this is a low-scoring affair that will be decided by a field goal. Verdict: Win Week 2: vs. Indianapolis Colts The Colts are essentially the same team as a year ago, sans wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. I thought the Colts were midseason “paper-tiger” champions last year, and I think the same this time around. Verdict: Win Week 3: at Miami Dolphins This is Kansas City’s first road game, and luckily it’s against a team that, by all accounts, seems to be tanking for Texas quarterback Arch Manning or someone similar. Not only is Malik Willis the starting quarterback, but the top two wide receivers had less than 550 yards combined in 2025. Verdict: Win Week 4: at Las Vegas Raiders I was born a Raider hater, and I’ll die one. I’d rather eat broken glass or French kiss a snapping turtle than pick the Raiders to win. Verdict: Win Week 5: BYE WEEK 4-0 Record! Week 6: vs. Los Angeles Chargers I can’t stand cheaters. So I can’t stand Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh. The Chargers have surrounded quarterback Justin Herbert with numerous offensive weapons, guys like running back Omarion Hampton or wide receiver Ladd McConkey. But if it’s one thing I know and believe in my heart, it’s that the Chargers are going to Charger and find a way to mess things up. Verdict: win Week 7: at Seattle Seahawks I don’t think the defending Super Bowl Champion Seahawks are unbeatable. In fact, on the contrary. I think the loss of Kenneth Walker will hurt this team more than it realizes. But I don’t think the Chiefs pull this one out. I may be a Homer, but I’m not disingenuous. Unfortunately, the Kenneth Walker revenge game comes up short. Verdict: lose Week 8: at Denver Hopefully our offensive line is healthy at this point in the season, and Patrick Mahomes is back or close to 100%. Even so, Denver’s defense is too good to let the Chiefs sweep them this season. Verdict: lose Week 9: vs New York Jets Chiefs fans get the Jets as a palate cleanser in week nine. I like the Jets’ young receivers and tight ends, but I’d be hard-pressed to pick a team led by quarterback Geno Smith to present too much of a threat in Arrowhead. Verdict: win Week 10: at Atlanta Falcons It doesn’t matter if it’s Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. playing quarterback, Atlanta’s offense will only go as far as running back Bijan Robinson can take them. Atlanta’s defense is mid, and I think the Chiefs can score on them. Verdict: win Week 11: vs. Arizona Cardinals This Cardinals team has one of the best starting skill position groups in the NFL, headlined by running back Jeremiyah Love, receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and tight end Trey McBride. Still, quarterback Jacoby Brissett might as well be named Geno Smith. Verdict: win Week 12: at Buffalo Bill s This is the biggest game of the season, hands down. Any time Mahomes and Bills quarterback Josh Allen face off, you have the makings of a game for the record books. I’m sticking to the historical pattern we’ve followed with Mahomes and Allen. Bills win the regular season game. The Chiefs win a postseason matchup. Verdict: lose Week 13: at Los Angeles Rams With defensive tackle Aaron Donald coming out of retirement to play with edge rusher Myles Garrett, I fully expect Mahomes to be running for his life. Verdict: los e Week 14: vs. Cincinnati Bengals This is going to be a fun year. We get to play all the teams we love to hate. I think the Bengals are going to be worse than Skyline Chili that’s been left out all night. Verdict: win Week 15: vs. New England Patriots Despite having an owner and a head coach who like to find themselves in the tabloids, the Patriots are still a really good team with Drake Maye at quarterback. Verdict: lose Week 16: vs. San Francisco 49ers I think the Chiefs bounce back here and jump on the 49ers early, repeating the results of Super Bowls LIV and LVIII. Verdict: win Week 17: at Los Angeles The Chargers are guests in their own stadium. The Chiefs will sweep the NFL’s redheaded stepchild. Verdict: win Week 18: vs. Raiders I hope the entire Raiders team gets shingles and they have to forfeit. Even if head coach Andy Reid is in a position to rest starters, I think the Chiefs still roll these scabs with ease. Verdict: win Final prediction: 12-5 (1st in the AFC West) There you have it. Tell me what a homer I am, and why I’m wrong in the comments below.

title: Chiefs’ Trey Smith: ‘You’re never going to feel 100% playing football’
summary: Kansas City Chiefs right guard Trey Smith missed part of last month’s training camp at Missouri Western State University with a hip ailment. full_text: Aug 28, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs guard Trey Smith (65) arrives prior to a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs right guard Trey Smith missed part of last month’s training camp at Missouri Western State University with a hip ailment. After being absent much of the camp’s second half — and being reported to have consulted with a hip specialist — Smith was able to be on the field for the first six offensive snaps of Kansas City’s preseason finale against the Seattle Seahawks . Smith spoke after Thursday’s practice. Echoing offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, the veteran discussed his mindset while off the field and what motivates him to return as quickly as possible. This is good stuff from Trey Smith here on a @SamMcDowell11 asked Question about begging to stay in during practices, even when he may not be 100%. Football player. pic.twitter.com/uRffmxdYNW — Harold R. Kuntz (@HaroldRKuntz3) September 3, 2026 “I just don’t like putting my teammates out in a position where now they’re trying to take extra reps or for me to leave my team hanging,” Smith explained. “Not being my best — a lot of times I’m a little hardheaded in that regard. If I’m not at my best, it’s not the best thing for the team. The other guys are willing and able to do it. I’ve always been sort of been a guy that’s like, ‘If I’m able to go, I’m going to try to go and give as much as I have regardless.‘ “You’re never going to feel 100% playing football. It’s just part of the job and part of the responsibility. Like EB says, we signed up for it. At the end of the day, I signed the contract, so it’s my job to be out there. A lot of times when I’m not out there, I feel like I’m not doing my job. I’m letting my team down for me [and] my coaches. I don’t like that feeling whatsoever.” Throughout camp, Smith found himself lined up next to a right tackle rotation of veteran Jaylon Moore and undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson. Regardless of which players he plays with against the Denver Broncos in Week 1, Smith has faith that offensive line coaches Andy Heck and Corey Matthaei will have that player ready — as well as anyone who may be called upon to fill in for an injured starter. “They both do a phenomenal job,” Smith remarked of Moore and Benson. “Coach Heck and Corey Matthaei do a fabulous job of teaching each and every one that goes out there. So, it’s always been a next up mentality. When I go out, the next man has to step up and do a great job. So, I have great chemistry with both those players and other guys that we’ve assembled here as well. We have to continue to just keep building and have a quantum of faith and confidence in them and the job our coaches do getting them prepared and ready to go.”

summary: Jim Harbaugh is going into his third season with the Los Angeles Chargers, hoping to finally get his team over the hump. The Chargers have made the playoffs in each of Harbaugh’s first two seasons, but have failed to get out of the wild card round, losing to the Houston Texans in 2024 and the […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers during warm up before a preseason game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jim Harbaugh is going into his third season with the Los Angeles Chargers, hoping to finally get his team over the hump. The Chargers have made the playoffs in each of Harbaugh’s first two seasons, but have failed to get out of the wild card round, losing to the Houston Texans in 2024 and the New England Patriots in 2025. Despite his playoff failures, Harbaugh is still considered to be one of the league’s top head coaches. The Chargers felt they needed to make some changes after last season’s disappointing loss against the Patriots. They fired offensive coordinator Greg Roman and replaced him with Mike McDaniel, who has served as the head coach of the Miami Dolphins for the past four seasons. Jesse Minter was also replaced by Chris O’Leary after he became the head coach of the Baltimore Ravens. Harbaugh has a 66-31-1 record across six seasons with the Chargers and San Francisco 49ers, and he’s been to the playoffs in all but one of those years. He has never finished below .500, which is also a sign that he is among the elite head coaches in the league. Harbaugh knows what it takes to lead a group of men, and he’s proven that in every stop he’s had in his career. The one thing that he doesn’t have on his resume is a Super Bowl win. The culture that he’s built within the Chargers has grown over the years, and it is a big reason why the team remains one of the best in the league since he arrived two years ago. If he can learn how to make the right changes and push the right buttons, he should be able to get the Chargers all the way to the Super Bowl.

title: Rams could have serious envy over this rookie receiver in season opener
summary: The Los Angeles Rams did not make a splash addition at wide receiver this offseason. There’s a chance it was because their guy got away. In a draft class with no shortage of uncertainties at the receiver position, one thing was known: teams from the Shanahan/McVay offensive tree would love De’Zhaun Stribling. Despite consensus boards […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: De'zhaun Stribling #15 of the San Francisco 49ers catches a deep pass over Cor'dale Flott #18 of the Tennessee Titans in the first half at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams did not make a splash addition at wide receiver this offseason. There’s a chance it was because their guy got away. In a draft class with no shortage of uncertainties at the receiver position, one thing was known: teams from the Shanahan/McVay offensive tree would love De’Zhaun Stribling. Despite consensus boards suggesting that the Ole Miss product would go somewhere closer to pick 100, the San Francisco 49ers grabbed him with the first selection in the second round (33rd overall). Now the Rams and 49ers are set to face off in Week 1. Los Angeles and Sean McVay may be unable to shake a feeling of envy that their division rivals just landed the next great receiver in this offensive scheme. LA should be pleased with its top two receivers. Puka Nacua may be the best pass catcher in the NFL. Davante Adams is still lethal, although it’s fair to question whether he can remain healthy for the full season. But behind Nacua and Adams, the depth chart gets shakier. You’d expect a little more potency from a team with Super Bowl expectations. There is also the matter of futureproofing, and the depth chart in 2027 looks bleak once you remove Adams. The Rams sat out all of free agency without making any additions at receiver. We know they would rather have Ty Simpson over the likes of Makai Lemon and Kenyon Sadiq. Instead Los Angeles—in somewhat of a surprise—went back to the tight end pool and selected Max Klare in the second round. Klare isn’t projected to have much of a role in 2026. Did McVay and Les Snead expect Stribling to be available in the back of round two? Despite appearing in only two preseason games, Stribling was targeted 13 times and caught 11 passes for 109 yards. He earned an elite and rookie class leading Pro Football Focus (PFF) offensive grade of 90.0. The 49ers may have drafted him too early compared to the media consensus, but the receiver is rewarded their confidence in him. Stribling will have his work cut out for him in his real NFL debut. He’ll line up against Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson in the Rams’ secondary. The 49ers’ receiving corps could also be fairly short-handed, and San Francisco may need their rookie ready right out of the gate. I’m not saying that the Rams should have taken De’Zhaun Stribling at thirteenth overall. Throwing a dart at the quarterback position is never a bad idea. The 49ers took their receiver far earlier than he was expected to be drafted, and now the Rams will see him twice per year. If Stribling becomes a star, that may be bad news for Los Angeles.

title: 49ers are facing adversity before season even begins
summary: While not the opening game, the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers will help kickoff the season on Thursday night in Melbourne, Australia. The 49ers are far from at full force. They are facing significant attrition and adversity before the new year even begins. Nick Bosa’s backups, Sam Okuayinonu and rookie Romello Height, did […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 13: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers walks on the field before a preseason NFL game against the Tennessee Titans on August 13, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images While not the opening game, the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers will help kickoff the season on Thursday night in Melbourne, Australia. The 49ers are far from at full force. They are facing significant attrition and adversity before the new year even begins. Nick Bosa’s backups, Sam Okuayinonu and rookie Romello Height , did not make the international trip. Bosa himself is recovering from last year’s ACL injury and tendinitis. Bosa himself will probably play . The bigger question is whether the star pass rusher will handle a full workload and/or look like himself. George Kittle—one of the best tight ends in football—tore his Achilles tendon in January. He’s trending in the direction of playing , but it’s difficult to imagine he’ll have a full workload. With a limited receiver corps, that we will get to in a second, not having Kittle at his best is a significant roadblock for the San Francisco offense. And then there are the receivers. Ricky Pearsall—someone the team expected to take a significant jump in year three—was shut down for the year. Christian Kirk, added in free agency as a footnote to their splash signing of Mike Evans, will start the season on injured reserve and miss at least the first four games. Evans missed most of training camp with an abductor, groin, quad injury and may also be on a limited pitch count similar to Bosa and Kittle. That leaves San Francisco with rookie De’Zhaun Stribling—the betting favorite to lead this year’s draft class in receiving yards—Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, and Jacob Cowing to catch passes from Brock Purdy. That list won’t exactly have a reloaded Rams secondary shaking in their boots, especially if Evans is limited or unavailable. This isn’t even the entire list. Last year’s overdrafted EDGE defender Mykel Williams will miss at least the first four games on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list. Safety Malik Mustapha is trending out of the Week 1 opener. Starting guard Dominick Puni suffered a concussion in camp and may not be ready in time. And all of this before we even mention Kyle Shanahan’s offseason adversity and the fact he might not be 100% at this point either. And, on top of that, have I mentioned that the 49ers will line up against Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, and Trent McDuffie? While the 49ers have a strong track record of winning under Shanahan, this seems to be a season where they at best finish in the middle of the pack. Their core has aged significantly and they were already players who were no strangers to injury. It’s hard to imagine San Francisco keeping Thursday’s game competitive. It’s even more difficult to think they can stave off the injury bug long enough to maintain a position in the playoff picture towards the end fo the year. The 49ers’ season may be over before it even begins.

title: Changes to HOF selection process could benefit Torry Holt
summary: The Pro Football Hall of Fame announced sweeping changes to its selection process that should benefit only Rams legend Torry Holt’s chances of making it to Canton. According to ESPN, these changes will include all eligible players in one category, instead of separating them into “modern era” and “senior” categories. This will come after the […]
full_text: ST. LOUIS, MO - DECEMBER 11: Torry Holt #81 of the St. Louis Rams runs with the ball while being tackled by Chris Harris #46 of the Chicago Bears on December 11, 2006 at the Edward Jones Dome Stadium in St. Louis, Missouri. (Photo by Sporting News via Getty Images via Getty Images) | Sporting News via Getty Images The Pro Football Hall of Fame announced sweeping changes to its selection process that should benefit only Rams legend Torry Holt’s chances of making it to Canton. According to ESPN , these changes will include all eligible players in one category, instead of separating them into “modern era” and “senior” categories. This will come after the mandatory five-year waiting period beginning with the 2027 class. The changes were made largely after Bill freaking Belichick, of all people, infamously didn’t get inducted into Canton in his first year of eligibility. The Pro Football Hall of Fame has made significant changes to the way it selects its annual classes, one year after Bill Belichick was snubbed in his first year of eligibility: Among the biggest changes: • Selection committee reduced from 50 members to 28. • Modern-Era… pic.twitter.com/eskdhrXoxW — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 4, 2026 These changes should be music to Holt’s ears, as he has waited far too long to receive his gold jacket. It’s made zero sense that one of the key members of the Greatest Show on Turf and one of the best wide receivers of his era isn’t in Canton. Keep in mind that Holt is the lone wideout on the NFL 2000s All-Decade Team not in the Hall of Fame. Marvin Harrison, Randy Moss and Terrell Owens are all in, just not the Rams’ icon, who is a seven-time finalist. With no disrespect intended towards Sterling Sharpe — who absolutely deserves to be in the HOF — it’s fair to wonder why Holt had to wait so long when his career production and longevity compare so favorably to the former Packers star. It shouldn’t have taken Belichick getting snubbed for changes to occur, since Holt had already spent years navigating a selection process that failed to reward his impressive resume. If players are going to be lumped into one category now, Holt should be right near the top of the list, even though at first glance, Steve Smith Sr. and Reggie Wayne, who are the most notable receiver candidates up for consideration, have the superior statistics. Holt (173 games): 920 receptions, 13,382 receiving yards, 74 touchdowns, 2 total All-Pro nods, one-time Super Bowl champ Wayne (211 games): 1,070 receptions, 14,345 receiving yards, 82 touchdowns, 3 total All-Pro nods, one-time Super Bowl champ Smith (219 games): 1,031 receptions, 14,731 receiving yards, 81 touchdowns, 4 total All-Pro nods While yes, Wayne and Smith have the better stats on paper, let’s put those numbers into context: Holt amassed his production in significantly fewer games. Holt played 46 fewer games than Smith, and 38 fewer than Wayne. That translates to about three seasons they had on Holt. His numbers don’t tell the full story, as he maintained near-equal, elite levels of production despite a shorter career. If the Rams icon played in over 210 games like Smith and Wayne, a simple per-game projection would’ve likely put him well above both players in receptions and receiving yards. There’s no guarantee that would’ve happened, of course, given injuries and what have you. Still, the stats prove how productive Holt was in the games he actually played. The waiting game on Holt’s Hall of Fame chances has undoubtedly been frustrating for Rams fans hoping to see him finally get inducted. There remains a logjam at wide receiver, with Wayne and Smith among Holt’s biggest competitors for enshrinement. Under the new system, though, he won’t be forced to wait behind a separate group of senior candidates who are only there because they’ve been waiting longer. This is exactly the break Holt has needed for years. Perhaps it’s finally time for one of the GSOT’s greatest contributors to join the rest of his teammates in Canton.

Top 100 Players of 2026, Nos. 10-1: Myles Garrett crowned after historic season, trade to Rams (nfl.com) “We’ve run out of superlatives for Garrett, who’s had quite the year. He set a new NFL single-season sack record on the way to his second Defensive Player of the Year honor , joining the likes of new teammate Aaron Donald (three), J.J. Watt (three), Lawrence Taylor (three), Ray Lewis (two), Bruce Smith (two), Reggie White (two), Mike Singletary (two) and Joe Greene (two) as players to win multiple DPOY awards. He belongs in that company after six straight Pro Bowls (seven total), five first-team All-Pro selections and eight consecutive seasons with double-digit sacks (he had seven in his rookie season). And yet, it’s possible that the elite edge rusher’s biggest win of the last 12 months was landing in Los Angeles this offseason via trade . He did everything in his power to elevate his former club in Cleveland, with two playoff appearances and a drawer full of individual accolades to show for it. Now in L.A., he has his first real shot at getting a ring.“ San Francisco 49ers arrive in Melbourne for historic NFL game against the LA Rams (newsday) “MELBOURNE, Australia — The San Francisco 49ers have arrived in Melbourne for their season-opening NFL game against the Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Sept. 11. It is expected to be the first of many regular-season NFL games in front of its growing Australian fan base.“ Rams release depth chart for Week 1 vs. 49ers (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams are just a week away from kicking off their 2026 season in Australia, starting the year with a rivalry game against the San Francisco 49ers. Their 53-man roster is set and on Thursday, the Rams released their first unofficial depth chart of the regular season. It’s much briefer than the preseason depth chart because there are 37 fewer players on it, and even though it’s unofficial, it’s still useful to see how the team looks heading into Week 1. While it’s not a direct reflection of how the coaching staff views starters and backups, it does show where the Rams are deepest and where they could use some more depth.“ Super Bowl LXI predictions: Los Angeles Rams lead seven NFL favorites to hoist Lombardi Trophy (nfl.com) “ Mike Band : Rams over Broncos. Sean Payton gets the most out of Bo Nix and a Broncos roster with no glaring weakness, but no team can match the Rams’ elite combination of quarterback, head coach and overall talent. Plus, this game is at SoFi Stadium. Jeremy Bergman : Rams over Chargers. Another Super Bowl at SoFi, another Rams win in the Rams House. Jim Harbaugh and Co.’s dream season ends at the hands of their neighbors, with Myles Garrett logging a game-record 4.5 sacks. Dan Parr : Rams over Broncos. As much as I’d like to pick the underdog, it’s hard to choose against the squad that could easily end up with the best offense and best defense in the league. The Rams exorcise the NFL dream team demons. Chad Reuter : Rams over Bills. The Bills finally get their chance to bring the Lombardi Trophy to Buffalo, but Matthew Stafford and Myles Garrett are too tough to beat at SoFi Stadium in The Big Game. Nick Shook : Rams over Bengals. Yes, we’ll run it back like it’s 2021 all over again. L.A. hosts another Super Bowl featuring the home team, which breaks the hearts of Bengals fans again in a fashion that might even include another Aaron Donald signature moment. Raza Umerani : Rams over Ravens. Lamar Jackson and the Ravens have a dream season, but the Rams buzzsaw is inevitable. Matthew Stafford walks off into the sunset as a champion. Mike Yam : Rams over Bills. The Rams spent the offseason grabbing headlines, and they somehow live up to the hype all season long. Superman Josh Allen gets grounded by a suffocating L.A. defense. Lance Zierlein : Rams over Texans. Defense rules the day, and the Rams kick a field goal to break a late tie, giving Myles Garrett his first Super Bowl win.“ 49ers announce defensive end Sam Okuayinonu will not play Thursday vs. Rams (nbcsports) “Okuayinonu was not on the team flight to Melbourne , but the 49ers originally indicated it was possible that he could make a later flight if he made progress in his recovery from a foot injury. Today, the 49ers announced that Okuayinonu will not play. Okuayinonu is an important part of the 49ers’ defense: Last year he started 12 games in the regular season and both playoff games. This year he’s expected to be a backup but get plenty of snaps in the defensive line rotation, when he gets healthy.“ Rams Need Matthew Stafford to Break This Concerning Trend to Win the Super Bowl (si.com) “In 2011, Stafford threw for 5,038 yards and 41 touchdowns with the Detroit Lions. The very next season, he threw for less than half that, with 20 touchdowns. During the Rams’ Super Bowl season in 2021, Stafford threw for 41 touchdowns once again. While he got injured in 2022, he was only on pace for 18.9 touchdowns that season. Last year, Stafford threw for a career-high 46 touchdowns. If the Rams are going to meet expectations in 2026, they can’t afford a massive drop-off from Stafford. Again, that isn’t to say that they need him to once again throw over 40 touchdown passes. However, it’s hard to see the Rams winning the Super Bowl if he only throws 20. He’ll need to throw at least 25 touchdown passes.“ How much will the Rams play Aaron Donald this season, and when will he debut? (ramblinfan) “Ultimately, he will be a full-fledged starter . But a safe guess places Donald at around 500-700 snaps this season. His workload will gradually intensify as he acclimates to life in the NFL trenches. If you need a player to compare him to, the best example is nose tackle Poona Ford, who logged 508 snaps in 2025. Rams’ cat-and-mouse tactics only serve to confuse 49ers’ Week 1 prep While questioning what he has left in the tank is reasonable, it risks overlooking just how dominant Donald was throughout his 2014-2023 career. In short, a fraction of Donald is better than 100 percent of many starting defensive linemen. The thing is, more and more analysts believe Donald may be an early-season decoy .“ Top 25 NFL free agents in 2027: Puka Nacua, George Pickens headline way-too-early list (nfl.com) “Nacua would already be paid long-term if not for his immaturity off the field. On it, he’s off to one of the best starts to a career for any receiver in league history.“ NFL’s top 10 defenses in 2026? Texans, Seahawks, Rams headline ranking; don’t sleep on Jags, Bucs (nfl.com) “Did anyone enjoy this past offseason more than Rams DC Chris Shula? In March, the team filled a longstanding need at cornerback by importing the Chiefs’ stout duo of Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson . In June, Los Angeles traded…

title: Raiders 2026: Game-by-game predictions for Klint Kubiak’s 1st year
summary: While there was plenty of conjecture of what would happen during the Las Vegas Raiders head coaching search, once the team zeroed in on Klint Kubiak, it wasn’t a matter of “if” but “when”. And once it was clear the offensive-minded young hotshot was the choice by Silver & Black brass, even the normally reserved […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 20: Head coach Klint Kubiak of the Las Vegas Raiders looks on from the sideline during the game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images While there was plenty of conjecture of what would happen during the Las Vegas Raiders head coaching search, once the team zeroed in on Klint Kubiak, it wasn’t a matter of “if” but “when”. And once it was clear the offensive-minded young hotshot was the choice by Silver & Black brass, even the normally reserved Kubiak couldn’t hide his enthusiasm for the gig. Case in point: Kubiak attempting to play coy after he helped the Seattle Seahawks win Super Bowl XX as offensive coordinator during an on-field interview with NFL Network. It was an on-the-spot answer to his NFL future with the hyped up “Hell yeah, I’m going.” when asked if the Raiders was indeed his next destination . Las Vegas did well to be both deliberate and patient in its coaching search and landed a prize catch in the coaching sweepstakes. Seattle offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak said he is “fired up” about taking the Las Vegas Raiders’ head coaching job. https://t.co/R02veMa1Jb — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) February 9, 2026 Perhaps the even-keeled and attention-to-detail approach Kubiak brings to the table is just what the Raiders need? A classic old-school grinder like his father Gary Kubiak, Klint isn’t one to make any bombastic claims that can be used as motivational ammunition by the opposition and/or mocked after the triumphant claims face plant in horrific fashion. The younger Kubiak brought his trusted lieutenants from Seattle to Las Vegas in offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko and offensive line coach Rick Dennison. The rookie head coach also brought in experienced assistants in Mike McCoy (assistant head coach), Mike Sullivan (quarterbacks coach), and Joe DeCamillis (special teams). Alongside Kubiak as neophyte play callers is Rob Leonard, who impressed the Raiders head coach that an ascension from defensive line coach/defensive run game coordinator to defensive coordinator occurred this offseason. General manager John Spytek added big-ticket free agents in March followed by bringing in promising prospects in the 2026 NFL Draft a month later to bolster a roster for Kubiak’s initial season as captain over the Silver & Black Express. While the offense is going to be much improved than what we saw from the 2025 rendition of the Raiders — ranked 32nd in points scored (241) and yards gained (4,168) — growing pains and a roster that’s at the beginning stages of a rebuild/reload have me prognosticating a 6-11 rookie season for the coaching neophytes Kubiak and Leonard. Raiders’ additions today: 🏈C Tyler Linderbaum: 3-years, $81M 🏈LB Quay Walker: 3-years, $40.5M 🏈LB Nakobe Dean: 3-years, $36M 🏈WR Jalen Nailor: 3-years, $35M 🏈Kwity Paye: 3-years, $48M 🏈CB Eric Stokes: 3-years, $30M 🏈DE Malcolm Koonce: 1-year, $11M 🏈Trade for CB Taron… https://t.co/CIAPDjQNyY — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) March 9, 2026 There will be tough lessons learned with Las Vegas having the seventh-hardest strength of schedule in the NFL. But those matchups against a fierce NFC and AFC West will provide the growing pains Kubiak and Spytek need as the Raiders proceed on the new era. Let’s take a look at the week-by-week schedule and results: Week 1 – vs. Miami Dolphins: Win Kubiak’s desert marauders kick off the 2026 campaign with a home win over Jeff Haley’s visiting Dolphins in a battle of two rookie head coaches. Veteran Kirk Cousins is his usual efficient self as Las Vegas picks up Kubiak’s first regular-season victory as an NFL head coach and at home, nonetheless. Week 2 – at Los Angeles Chargers: Loss Jim Harbaugh and Mike McDaniel combine to create a formidable offense that wears down Leonard’s defense in this AFC West matchup. With the defense unable to get off the field, it leaves Kubiak’s offense little opportunity to operate resulting in a defeat. Week 3 – at New Orleans Saints: Loss Much like Las Vegas, New Orleans is on Year 2 of a rebuild under Kellen Moore — another hotshot young play caller given the reins of a football team. It’s a competitive game between the two teams but a missed field goal by Las Vegas turns out to be the difference maker. Matt Gay credits Joe DeCamillis for his growth, and now they’re back together in Vegas. https://t.co/9Qv4xifklG — Las Vegas Raiders (@Raiders) March 11, 2026 Week 4 – vs. Kansas City Chiefs: Loss Welcoming the always formidable Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes, the Chiefs cut through the Raiders like hot knife through butter in another early-season AFC West showdown. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo makes life tough for Kubiak and Cousins while Leonard struggles to contain the Chiefs’ offense. Week 5 – at New England Patriots: Loss Seething from both their postseason exit and the Week 1 loss at home to the Raiders in 2025, the Patriots fire on all cylinders to lap a Raiders team that has trouble in all three phases of the game on the road. Mike Vrabel’s football team is just too physical in this matchup. Week 6 – vs. Buffalo Bills: Loss Facing the trio of quality starting quarterbacks gives Leonard great teach tape but the Josh Allen-led Bills offense gets the best of the Raiders defense. Joe Brady has Buffalo’s offensive attack humming while Jim Leonhard devices ways to get after Cousins. Week 7 – vs. Los Angeles Rams: Loss Sean McVay and Matt Stafford are the latest to light up Leonard’s Raiders defense and despite Maxx Crosby being a constant harrier, Las Vegas’ offense can’t keep up with the high-octane attack the Rams bring to Allegiant Stadium. Week 8 – at New York Jets: Win A six-game skid snapped! Learning brutal lessons against some of the best offenses the NFL has to offer shows dividends as Leonard brings the heat. And that pressure against Jets quarterback Geno Smith leads to multiple takeaways and the Raiders offense capitalizes. Geno Smith in His First Preseason Action Back With the Jets: 7/7, 65 YDS, 1 TD, 0 INT, 144.9 Rating pic.twitter.com/YfYfJr50Bn — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) August 22, 2026 Week 9 – at San Francisco 49ers: Loss From the substation and injuries to head coach Kyle Shanahan’s car accident, to owner Jed York’s arrest the offseason has been one to forget for the Niners. But they have the coach and roster to get a home win over the developing Raiders. Week 10 – vs. Seattle Seahawks: Loss Want to see the type of defense we should eventually see with Leonard calling the plays? This is the game to see it as Mike Macdonald will have his Seahawks grabbing Kubiak’s Raiders offense by the throat and squeezing. Las Vegas will get its licks in, just not the W. Week 11 – vs. Denver Broncos: Loss Winless in Mile High since the 2022 season, the determined Broncos must stack as many victories it can in a competitive AFC West. This one will be a slugfest but a special teams gaffe costs the Raiders in the initial meeting between division foes. Week 12 – at Cleveland Browns: Win Shedur Sanders or Deshaun Watson, doesn’t matter. The Raiders defense rises to the occasion as Crosby and Co. rack up multiple sacks as tight end Brock Bowers showcases why he’s an elite young talent in the league with a multiple touchdown reception outing. Week 13 – Bye Week At 3-9 heading into a later hiatus week, Kubiak and Co. make a key decision pivot at quarterback. Comp update: Kirk Cousins will sign a five-year, $172 million deal with the Raiders that in reality is a one-year, fully-guaranteed $20 million deal that also contains a club option for two years at $80M. The Falcons will pay Cousins $8.7 million this season, the Raiders another… pic.twitter.com/MHYqOOfBs7 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) April 2, 2026 Week 14 – vs. Los Angeles Chargers: Loss Despite the plan of sit and learn minority owner Tom Brady has for the Raiders’ prized No. 1 overall selection…

title: Jeremiah Smith, Will Echoles, 2027 NFL draft wide receivers and defensive tackles Las Vegas Raiders fans should know
summary: While the Las Vegas Raiders settled in on their initial 53-man roster this week, there are a couple of glaring holes at wide receiver and defensive tackle heading into the season. Of course, players on the current roster can step up and fill them. But until then, those positions look like the two biggest needs […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - DECEMBER 31: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes celebrates after scoring a fourth quarter touchdown against the Miami Hurricanes during the 2025 College Football Playoff Quarterfinal at the 90th Goodyear Cotton Bowl Classic at AT&T Stadium on December 31, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Las Vegas Raiders settled in on their initial 53-man roster this week, there are a couple of glaring holes at wide receiver and defensive tackle heading into the season. Of course, players on the current roster can step up and fill them. But until then, those positions look like the two biggest needs the Raiders will have heading into the offseason and the 2027 NFL draft. With a gap between the end of training camp/the preseason and Week 1 in the NFL , College Football gets to take center stage this weekend. So, now is a great time to get an early jump on a few draft prospects at receiver and defensive tackle who Raider Nation will want to keep tabs on this fall. Wide Receivers Jeremiah Smith, Ohio State 2025 Stats: 87 catches, 1,243 yards, 12 TDs To be honest, if you don’t know who Jeremiah Smith is by now, you’re probably living under a rock. He’s been the best wide receiver in the country since he was an 18-year-old freshman two years ago. The 6-foot-3, 223-pound wideout has already drawn comparisons to Julio Jones with his size, speed and route-running combination. Jeremiah Smith is generational. pic.twitter.com/B3bPpv5pIC — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) April 28, 2026 Cam Coleman, Texas 2025 Stats: 56 catches, 708 yards, 5 TDs While the Auburn transfer doesn’t have eye-catching production so far in his career, that says more about the quarterback play he was working with than his skill set. However, that changes with Arch Manning slinging Coleman the rock this season. At 6-foot-3 and 197 pounds, he also has good size and can win down the field. If Smith is Julio Jones, then Coleman is A.J. Green, who ended up being the first receiver taken in the 2011 draft. New Texas WR Cam Coleman (formerly at Auburn) runs every vertical route like he hit the rainbow strip. Really excited to see how he develops with the Longhorns. pic.twitter.com/rNh2UmZWUX — Tyler Brooke (@TylerDBrooke) May 8, 2026 Nick Marsh, Indiana 2025 Stats: 59 catches, 662 yards, 6 TDs Despite both playing for Indiana, Marsh doesn’t have any connection to Fernando Mendoza after spending the first two years of his college career at Michigan State. But the former Spartan/current Hoosier is the type of receiver Mendoza and the Raiders need. “Marsh is a big (6’3″, 213 lbs), smooth and physical wide receiver, who can occupy the X-receiver role,” Bleacher Report’s Damian Parson said. “The 19-year-old target has the ability and potential to develop into a long-term WR1.” New Indiana WR Nick Marsh is such a bully. 6'3" 203 pounds. Play strength shows up in his routes, after the catch, and as a PLUS plus blocker. pic.twitter.com/0Q5B44pU7c — Tyler Brooke (@TylerDBrooke) May 31, 2026 Ryan Coleman-Williams, Alabama 2025 Stats: 49 catches, 689 yards, 4 TDs Coleman-Williams was a freshman sensation two years ago but was plagued by drops last season, letting 10 passes slip through his hands. That was the third-most among FBS wideouts according to Pro Football Focus . But if the former 5-star recruit can fix that problem, he’d be a good fit in Klint Kubiak’s offense with his versatility to win from the slot or out wide and make plays after the catch. Ryan Coleman-Williams has RARE athletic gifts… hoping for a big 2026 season 👀 pic.twitter.com/oLZPbS2gpg — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) July 23, 2026 Bryant Wesco Jr., Clemson 2025 Stats: 31 catches, 537 yards, 6 TDs Last season, Wesco was on the verge of having a breakout campaign, averaging 76.7 yards per game through seven contests before a scary back/neck injury prematurely sidelined him. The 6-foot-2, 195-pound pass catcher is fully healthy now and has the speed to be a legitimate vertical threat at the next level. Bryant Wesco Jr. is a 1st round talent if he stays healthy in 2026 Ridiculous blend of speed, quickness, and route running ability pic.twitter.com/Oa0p56K8oT — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) August 17, 2026 Charlie Becker, Indiana 2025 Stats: 34 catches, 679 yards, 4 TDs If you watched Mendoza down the stretch of Indiana’s National Championship run last year, then you certainly got a glimpse of what Becker can bring to the table. The former roommates had great chemistry together and connected on several deep passes, as the wideout led the Big 10 with 20.0 yards per catch. Becker didn’t start until Week 9 last year, making it even more interesting to see what he can do with a bigger workload in 2026. Charlie Becker 6 REC, 126 YDS vs OSU Today in the Big Ten Championship. pic.twitter.com/l4luUjbRfz https://t.co/5awjeBfAHM — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) December 7, 2025 Defensive Tackles Will Echoles, Ole Miss 2025 Stats: 68 tackles, 5 sacks, 11.5 TFLs Echoles heads into the campaign as the top defensive tackle in the class for what he brings as a run defender. The 6-foot-3, 315-pounder has the size, strength and athleticism to defeat any type of block and be a constant presence in the offense’s backfield. He’s still putting it all together to be a more consistent pass-rusher, but five sacks and 39 pressures, per PFF , last season is good production to build on. Echoles also had six batted passes a year ago to impact the passing game beyond getting to the quarterback. Will Echoles | IDL | Ole Miss | 6-3, 309 Well rounded, disruptive DT. Active hands, explosive power, and finishing ability. Just turned 20 years old this week. pic.twitter.com/c2AVb9uNgj — Jordan Reid (@Jordan_Reid) August 8, 2026 David Stone, Oklahoma 2025 Stats: 42 tackles, 1.5 sacks, 8 TFLs With only two career starts heading into this season, Stone is more of a projection at this stage. However, he did play over 450 snaps last year and proved to be a very impressive run defender while showing some intriguing athletic traits. The Oklahoma native’s recruiting profile states he has nearly 35-inch arms, per 247Sports’ Andrew Ivins , and he moves well to grow as a pass-rusher down the line. Oklahoma DT David Stone is so damn quick off the snap, but he's also so hard to displace. Really, really good DT prospect who has a real chance at being an early first-round pick. pic.twitter.com/imOMbMOKNy — Tyler Brooke (@TylerDBrooke) June 18, 2026 A’Mauri Washington, Oregon 2025 Stats: 33 tackles, 1.5 sacks, 4.5 TFLs Washington likely would have been a second-round pick—maybe even a late first-rounder—had he declared for the draft last season. Instead, the Oregon product returned to school, where he’ll look to turn athletic potential into pass-rush production this fall. Regardless, the 6-foot-3, 325-pounder is a force in the running game with the combination of strength at the point of attack and agility to effectively take away two gaps. Was putting off watching #Oregon DL A'Mauri Washington until this game and he is really, really impressive physically Strong, powerful, explosive. Crazy get-off that puts @BruceFeldmanCFB 's crazy numbers from the 'Freaks List' on display Scary that his best ball is ahead of him pic.twitter.com/HFtI54aPI7 — Fran Duffy (@FDuffyNFL) September 28, 2025 Ahmad Moten, Miami 2025 Stats: 31 tackles, 4.5 sacks, 9 TFLs With a quick first step, Moten is a gap-shooter who can consistently get penetration in both phases of the game. He’s different than the other defensive tackles listed here as more of a disruptor than someone who can hold his gap consistently against the run. Also, the Hurricane is the most polished pass-rusher of the bunch, right now. David Stone is my early DT #1, but Ahmad Moten from Miami is right there really close behind him for me. This guy is super explosive off the snap, had 4.5 sacks in 2025, and also had a 74.3 run defense grade. pic.twitter.com/aqz28foLAh — Bengals & Brews…
